articleTitle: WiFi band-stop FSS for increased privacy protection in smart building
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a periodic double ring strip frequency selective surface (FSS) with dual-band stop behavior. The FSS elements are designed to be etched on the transparent coating of glass substrate in smart buildings, which acts as a dual-band notch filter on 2.45GHz and 5.4GHz to avoid the leakage of WiFi signal outside the building. All the simulation parts are simulated by using High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS). The proposed FSS possesses 450MHz and 960MHz bandwidth with insertion loss more than -10dB around the two central operating frequencies 2.45GHz and 5.45GHz, respectively. Furthermore, the unit-cell structure provides a stable performance for both TE and TM polarizations with incident angles 0°-60°. A prototype of the proposed FSS is fabricated and measured. Good agreement between the simulated and measured results is obtained.

articleTitle: Low-complexity interference cancellation receiver for sparse code multiple access
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Sparse code multiple access (SCMA) is a proposed candidate for multiple access method in 5G telecommunication. In SCMA system, the classic receiver is message passing algorithm (MPA). MPA can reach a near optimal performance, but the computation process is complicated and time-consuming, so MPA is suitable for advanced terminal. But for simple terminal such as sensor node, large mount of calculations are difficult to bear. In this paper, we propose two interference cancellation (IC) related receivers to reduce complexity, including serial interference cancellation (SIC) and jointed serial interference cancellation with MPA algorithm (Jointed SIC-MPA). It's important to emphasize that these two IC related algorithms are designed jointed with multi-dimensional modulation constellation design. We propose a new method to generate multi-dimensional constellation. Both of them have lower complexity compared with classic MPA receiver.

articleTitle: Use modified Lomb-Scargle method to analyze electromagnetic emission spectrum
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Analyzing the harmonic component from emission spectrum is an effective method to find emission source in trouble-shooting for electronic system. In some situations, to improve test efficiency, different frequency steps may be used in different bands and the emission spectrum may be unevenly spaced in different bands. Moreover, the possible environmental interferences and data missing are difficulty for analysis. A novel method using modified Lomb-Scargle periodogram to extracting the base-frequency feature is presented in this paper. In this method, segmentation multi-resolution analysis is used as a preprocessing method to separate the harmonic component and broadband component. Modified Lomb-Scargle periodogram is used to extract the base-frequency features next. Several simulation and experimental results in different situations are demonstrated then. The results show that the proposed method can extract the base-frequency features effectively from unevenly spaced frequency spectrum which may have several environmental interferences and some data missing.

articleTitle: A compact omnidirectional CP coaxial slots antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this letter, a compact omnidirectional CP coaxial slots antenna with high gain and omnidirectional circularly polarized (CP) performance is presented. The antenna is based on the coaxial cylinder structure, and the omnidirectional CP property is realized by perpendicular slot pairs surrounding the coaxial cylinder symmetrically on the out conductor. Slots are constructed as slot array to ensure its high gain performance. The antenna is left hand circularly polarized (LHCP) and works at 5GHz frequency band.

articleTitle: A modified UWB antipodal Vivaldi antenna with improved radiation characteristics
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a modified antipodal Vivaldi antenna is presented for UWB applications. To extend the low-end bandwidth limitation and improve the radiation characteristics in the lower frequencies, a novel elliptical slot edge (ESE) structure is employed. The addition of ESE structure helps the antenna lower the low-end operating frequency by 570 MHz with the dimension unaltered. In addition, a pair of planar directors is used to improve the value of gains at high frequency bands. The proposed antenna achieves a −10 dB |S11| with bandwidth of 1.69–11 GHz and demonstrates good unidirectional radiation patterns over the operating frequency band with peak gain values in the range of 4.13–11.48 dBi.

articleTitle: Design of a novel multi-layered eighth-mode substrate integrated waveguide filter by HFSS
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In order to solve the miniaturization of the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filter, a novel multi-layered eighth-mode substrate integrated waveguide filter is proposed. The filter is designed and simulated by high frequency structure simulator (HFSS).The simulated result shows that the dimensions are reduced almost 87.5% and it has a good property with bandwidth about 23.3%,which realize the miniaturization of the filter.

articleTitle: A compact and anti-interference filter-antenna for modern wireless communication systems
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a compact and anti-interference filter-antenna is designed for modern wireless communication systems. This filter-antenna consists of a microstrip rectangular open-loop resonator, a coupling line and a Γ-shaped antenna. The Γ-shaped antenna is excited by coupled line. Meanwhile, the coupled line is used as an admittance converter in filter design. The Γ-shaped antenna not only plays the role of radiation, but also the filter last resonator. The advantage of this design is that there is no loss between the filter and the antenna. The measured results show that the filter-antenna impedance bandwidth of the reflection coefficient S11<− 10dB is 12.7% (2.36–2.68GHz).

articleTitle: Dual-band antenna and high efficiency rectifier for RF energy harvesting system
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we present a simple dual-band patch antenna that radiates at 920MHz and 2.4GHz effectively. The patch antenna is designed with meander slot and shorting probe to increase the current path and reduce the resonant frequency. In addition, a high efficiency, dual-band rectifier is also proposed here. The rectifier is designed by a four-stage voltage doubler topology with lump inductors added, and the resonant frequency can be tuned independently. At an input power level of 15dBm, the experimental result shows a RF-to-DC conversion efficiency up to 78% at dual-band can be achieved. The corresponding DC output voltage is 7.26V and 6.82V respectively with a 9.1kOhm load.

articleTitle: Research on the transmission and coupling issue of multilayer TSV and multilayer TSV array
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Since more chips are fabricated within 3D-IC, the single layer TSV cannot satisfy the requirement. Hence, the multilayer TSV structure was proposed, and the influence of different bump radius, bump height, underfill material in the intermetallic layer on the TSV performance was studied. In reality, multilayer TSV array is applied in the product. Therefore two multilayer 4 × 4 TSV arrays have been proposed with different GS distribution. The coupling analysis was performed and the effect of ground TSV was studied.

articleTitle: Research on unwanted reflections in an OATS for precise omni antenna measurement
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Open-area test site (OATS) is a basic facility for measuring omni-directional antennas at VHF/HUF band. Usually, the reflections from the trees nearby, from the edge of the metal ground plane of an OATS are detrimental to precise omni-directional antenna measurements from 20 MHz to 1 GHz; however they are very difficult to quantify accurately, since no rigorous theory on the relationship between the reflections and the configurations of an OATS. In order to study these unwanted reflections, a pair of precise ultra-broadband calculable dipole antennas (CDAs) are developed and verified with a slightly modified near-field method, whose site-insertion-loss deviation (ΔSIL) between measurements and simulation is less than 0.3 dB from 10 MHz to 340 MHz for a single pair of dipoles resonated at 90 MHz; then the effects of ground plane sizes, wire mesh shapes around the edge of the metal ground plane, trees nearby are researched. The research shows that these unwanted reflections from the edge of an optimized ground plane is less than 0.1 dB at 10 m range. Finally, the performance of an optimized OATS is validated: for 10 m separation, ΔSIL is within 0.26 dB at horizontal polarization (HP) and within 0.34 dB at vertical polarization (VP) for the typical 24 frequencies from 30 MHz to 1 GHz; at 20 m separation, ΔSIL is within 0.59 dB (HP) and 0.85 dB (VP) from 20 MHz to 500 MHz. An uncertainty of calibrating tuned dipole antennas are provided, too.

articleTitle: A Ka-band transceiver module based on LTCC technology
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A Ka-band low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) transceiver is demonstrated in this paper. The proposed module is composed of several bare monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMIC) and passive circuits. These MMICs including LNA, phase shifter, attenuator, SPDT switch, driver amplifier, power amplifier have been mounted onto LTCC substrate. The passive circuits like bandpass filter and waveguide to microstrip transition have been embedded into the substrate. The whole transceiver is fabricated in a 36mm×20mm×1.1mm LTCC board with eleven layers. The front-end is designed to operate from 34 to 36 GHz. Measurement shows that the gain of the receiver is 33 dB; noise figure is less than 4.2 dB. Output power of transmitter is greater than 24.6 dBm, while the measured gain is more than 25 dB. The implementation of this transceiver indicates that LTCC technology is well suited for highly integrated microwave and millimeterwave module.

articleTitle: UFMC system performance analysis for discrete narrow-band private networks
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the performance of universal-filtered multi-carrier (UFMC) system is analyzed. Specifically, the UFMC signals are generated with Dolph-Chebyshev, Hamming and Hanning filtering. The characteristics of UFMC signals are also compared with OFDM signal, in both software and hardware-in-the-loop simulations. Experimental results show that UFMC signals have better performance than OFDM signal, by means of side-lobe attenuation, bit-error-ratio (BER) and Error Vector Magnitude (EVM). The results indicate that the UFMC signal is more suitable than OFDM signal for discrete narrow-band private networks. The results can provide useful information on the design of multi-carrier radio systems.

articleTitle: A design of miniaturization LPDA antenna with ultra wideband
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper designed a Log-periodic miniaturization antenna working in 8GHz to 18GHz. It satisfies the characteristic of high gain, good radiation pattern, and a large proportion of the size reduction which other antenna don't possess. The lengthwise is 80mm, it reduces more than 50% of the transverse dimension with the original specification. A “mountain” terminal loaded design is used to shrink size of antenna under the premise of guaranteeing directivity of antenna. By optimizing backward feeding structure and antenna array to improve antenna performance. The final result is superior to other same type antenna distinctly.

articleTitle: The design of high gain and miniaturization microstrip antenna array for RFID reader
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low gain for traditional RFID microstrip antenna, this paper has designed a 2×2 microstrip antenna array with simple structure, integration, miniaturization and a center work frequence of 2.45GHz. The antenna array adopts coaxial cable as the feeder and a simple impedance matching network is designed which is composed of some T-shaped structure to match with 50 ohm coaxial line. The results of simulation and experimental show that the maximum gain of antenna is 13.9dB.

articleTitle: Parameters analysis of Gaussian pulse circuit based on avalanche transistors
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Marx circuit based on avalanche transistors could be used to produce high power-nanosecond-Gaussian pulse. In this paper, theoretical calculations and software simulation of circuit parameters on the impact of the pulse waveform parameters are analyzed. The results show us that the charging voltage mainly affect amplitude and rise time of the pulse generated, the charging capacitor mainly impact the amplitude and fall time of the pulse, charging resistors could limit the maximum pulse repetition frequency. This paper provides a theoretical reference for the selection of components in the design of pulse source circuit and the researches of adjustable Gaussian pulse source.

articleTitle: Wideband RCS reduction of slot antenna array by using reflectarrays
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: According to the principle of reflectarray, this paper presents a new way which disperses the scattered energy into different directions to reduce the RCS of the slot antenna array, preserving its radiating performance at the same time. Four reflectarrays are designed using double square ring elements of variable size, and they are loaded onto the patch side of the slot antenna array by region. The reflectarrays disperse the scattering field into different directions, which makes a significant reduction of monostatic RCS in a wide frequency band including in-band and out-band. The backward RCS of the slot antenna array with reflectarrays can be reduced as much as 20dBsm compared to that of the conventional antenna array.

articleTitle: A compact Vivaldi antenna with triple band-notched characteristics
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a compact Vivaldi antenna with triple notchband is designed. Three stepped-impedance resonator (SIR) structures are introduced into a Vivaldi antenna to creating triple band-notched characteristics. Comparing with the antenna that only has one notch band, the triple band notched antenna proposed in this paper can reject more narrowband applications. In addition, the passband would be less affected by the notch band due to the sharp transition band between notched band and operating band. The simulated and measured results demonstrate that the Vivaldi antenna realizes an impedance bandwidth from 3.1GHz to 10.6GHz at S11<−10dB except the bandwidth of 3.3GHz∼3.8GHz for WIMAX and 5.15GHz∼5.35GHz, 5.725GHz∼5.825GHz for WLAN. Good direction ensures that it can be used for directional UWB applications.

articleTitle: Design of a tri-band MIMO antenna with high isolation for WLAN and WiMAX applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A tri-band MIMO antenna operating in WLAN 2.4/5.2/5.8GHz bands and WiMAX 2.5/3.5/5.5GHz bands is presented in this paper. The proposed MIMO antenna consists of two CPW-fed antenna elements and a P-shaped patch. The two antenna elements have high isolations which are over 28dB in the WLAN 5.2/5.8GHz bands and WiMAX 3.5/5.5GHz bands and over 30 dB in the WLAN 2.4GHz band and WiMAX 2.5GHz band. The high isolations are achieved by arranging the two CPW-fed antennas perpendicularly and adding the additional parasitic element (the P-shaped patch) between the two elements. The return loss, isolation, current distribution and radiation patterns of the proposed MIMO antenna are investigated by using HFSS software. The results show that the proposed MIMO antenna can cover the whole WLAN and WiMAX bands and has good isolation characteristic, which can well meet the WLAN and WiMAX applications.

articleTitle: Design of a UWB unidirectional radiation compound spiral antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The design of a modified unidirectional radiation miniaturized compound spiral antenna fed by an exponentially tapered balun is shown in this paper. The compound spiral antenna is designed by combining a typical equiangular spiral antenna with Archimedean spiral line. By taking advantage of a modified reflector to make the antenna into a microstrip form, the structure realizes a typical unidirectional radiation pattern for planar spiral antennas, which naturally increases radiation gain. In the range from 5 to 20 GHz, simulated radiation patterns, axial ratio plots and VSWR plots show good performance. The comparison with the compound spiral antenna and traditional UWB antennas shows the improvement of the axial ratio.

articleTitle: Studies on circular array interferometer direction finding
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: First of all, this paper analyzes the short baseline interferometer direction finding and gets the shortcoming of this direction finding. As the following, the paper analyzes the long/short baseline direction finding and the direction finding based on L array. After, we give the analysis of the circular array interferometer direction finding and the theory of antenna array. At the end, we make a test of this direction finding.

articleTitle: Modeling method of electromagnetic environment prediction
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic environment prediction refers to forecast the developing trend of electromagnetic environment in future based on forecast model. Through the research on the constitute and the dynamic characteristics of electromagnetic environment, according to electromagnetic environment simulation process and external interference electromagnetic environment, mutual interference, dynamic characteristics of the electromagnetic environment faced by electronic information equipment, external interference model, the internal mutual interference model and the dynamic control model of electromagnetic environment are established. At last, according to the electromagnetic environment simulation and prediction, multi point receiving simulation method are put forward and the simulation process is established, which provide support for electromagnetic environment prediction research. Comparison of simulation and outdoor experiments show that the prediction models and methods described herein improve the efficiency and accuracy of prediction of the electromagnetic environment.

articleTitle: A wide angle 3D ADI-PE scheme for radio wave propagation prediction in tunnels
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A wide angle three dimensional parabolic equation with impedance boundary condition (IBC) for radio wave propagation prediction in tunnel environment is presented, which is solved by the Alternate Direction Implicit (ADI) method. The proposed method with the Pade polynomial approximation expands the applicable angle of parabolic equation method to 30°, which is suitable for predicting the radio propagation in the tunnel with wide beam width. The simulation results indicate that the proposed method remains the advantages of the narrow angle scheme (less than 15°) accuracy and improves the accuracy of wide angle scheme.

articleTitle: A novel ultra-wide band omnidirectional antenna with lightweight design
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel ultra-wide band (UWB) omnidirectional antenna with lightweight design is proposed. By combining the advantageous characteristics of disc monopole antenna and bi-conical antenna as well as further structure optimization, the proposed antenna is featured with omnidirectional radiation in ultra-wide band. Furthermore, by using linearized metal wire, the size of designed antenna is minimized to 270mm × 270mm × 291.5 mm, which is significantly lightweight. Also, the simulation results demonstrate that the antenna can work from 0.23GHz to 5.2 GHz with low return loss and has relatively high gain omnidirectionally in the whole band.

articleTitle: A novel triple notch-bands UWB band-pass filter using E-shaped resonator and open-load stubs
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A novel triple notch-bands UWB (ultra-wide band) band-pass filter with three sharply rejected notched bands based on E-shaped resonator and open-load stubs was proposed in this paper. The basic UWB BPF was designed using stepped impedance resonator (SIR) and four short-circuited stubs with length of λ/4.To achieve triple band-notched performance, the proposed triple notch-bands UWB BPF used E-shaped resonator and two open-load stubs to couple to the stepped impedance resonator (SIR) of the basic UWB BPF. The simulation results showed that the proposed filter with triple band notched at 4.8 GHz,6.6GHz and 9.4 GHz. The proposed filter can realize sharp out-of-band rejection performance and the maximum ripple was 0.88 dB, while the minimum insertion loss was 0.6dB.

articleTitle: Design of wide band directional coupler by ridged rectangular waveguide for large power capability
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: By the theory of Bethe-hole coupling, a new modified multi-hole directional coupler based on the ridged rectangular waveguide is proposed in this paper. Three kinds of coupling-hole configurations, namely, circular hole, triangle hole and square hole, are investigated for realizing the wide band coupling between two different transmission lines. After extensive simulation and analysis, square hole is chosen as it exhibits best bandwidth performance. The coupling coefficient is 40 dB with a deviation smaller than 2 dB. The proposed coupler can be a promising candidate for application scenarios where flat coupling, high directivity, high power capacity and broad band width properties are desired.

articleTitle: Analysis on the characteristics of radiation emission of EMU
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The radiation emission of trains must be concerned to ensure its safe operation. In this paper, the radiation emission of EMU under different working conditions is explored. The radiation emission is tested when EMU passes through the test point by the speed of 50 kilometers per hour in accordance with the standard of the 3-level traction and 3-level braking. Test result shows that radiation emission exceeded the limit at frequency 9kHz-11MHz. Radiation emission of other frequency range is qualified. Then the traction system of a certain type of EMU is analyzed to find the cause of exceeding radiation. From the test results, it can be judged that the source of the disturbance is traction converter. The traction system is introduced to explore the reason of exceeding radiation emission. Some way towards the traction converter is suggested to suppress the radiation emission, and showed the suppressing effect.

articleTitle: Study on carrier cancellation in UHF RFID test system
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: First, the UHF RFID tag test system is introduced in the paper and the carrier leakage issue in the test system had been illustrated. Then the paper analyzed the effect of carrier leakage impacting tag test. And the solution had been given that designing the carrier cancellation circuit before the receiver in order to suppress the leakage RF power. The circuit should adjust the amplitude of transmitting carrier to equal the receiving carrier and adjust the phase reverse to receiving carrier. The adjustment of circuit should complete automatically and quickly enough. At the end the test had been implemented and the data result had verified the actual effect of carrier cancellation.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband 20-way coaxial power combiner
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper we present a new ultra-wideband 20-way coaxial power combiner. In this new structure, there is a radially extended coaxial cavity and 20 coaxial coupling probes. It can not only be used as power combiner but also power divider. There are several critical parameters we'll discuss here that ultimately determine the performance of the new power combiner. The new structure can efficiently work in ultra-wideband 6GHz-18GHz range. ANSYS HFSS simulation results show that the insertion loss is less than -1dB and the return loss is below -15dB. With relatively compacted body, space is sufficiently used and manufacturing process is easy for industry production.

articleTitle: Behavioral modeling and simulation of electromagnetic interference response for radio frequency receiver
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a behavior modeling method of electromagnetic interference response for the radio frequency receiver is presented by studying the main modules, including amplifiers, filters and mixers. The key technology of accurate modeling approaches for nonlinear effects of amplifiers and mixers is developed for a better prediction accuracy. The model of the receiver is then used in the research for interference response laws of the amplifier to interference signal with different parameters involving power, bandwidth and center frequency deviation compared to that of the receiver.

articleTitle: Ka/W dual frequency band dual polarization horn antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A Ka/W dual frequency band (35 and 95 GHz) dual polarization horn antenna with low cross polarization and high isolation is proposed in this paper. The realization of the dual linearly-polarization antenna is by two orthogonal coupled feed windows in each transmission waveguide. We realize the good radiation pattern of the dual frequency band by corrugated horn, which has compact structure and easy to manufacture. In addition, the realization of high isolation between two frequency band is by adding a band-pass filter at the Ka feed waveguide. The simulation results show that the antenna has good radiation pattern, low cross polarization level and high port isolation. The cross polarization level is lower −34 dB in both frequency bands. The isolation between the two frequency bands is better than a high degree of 100 dB to limit the interference of the signals.

articleTitle: A method of Markov channel modeling for reentry dynamic plasma sheath
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In order to investigate the effect of dynamical plasma sheath on communication signals, this paper proposes band finite-state Markov channel model to represent the dynamic plasma effect on signals at Ka band. First, the amplitude attenuation characteristics induced by dynamic plasma are calculated by Transmission Line Analogy method. Then the Ka band finite-state Markov channel model of dynamic plasma sheath is established according to the attenuation statistical characteristic and equal distance (ED) state partition method is proposed. Simulation results show that the first order statistical channel properties of the proposed channel model agree with the original attenuation data well. Finally, BER performance of typical telemetry, track and command (TT&C) signals under the established model is analyzed as well.

articleTitle: Active frequency selective surfaces for beam switching applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a beam switching antenna with a novel active frequency selective surface (AFSS) is proposed at 5.2 GHz. The antenna is composed of an omnidirectional patch antenna and AFSS. The AFSS is made up of 6 columns, each with 2 unit cells, which are placed vertically around a patch antenna to form a hexagonal wall. To steer beam of the antenna, high frequency pin diodes are precisely inserted into the AFSS to reconfigure electromagnetic (EM) response of surfaces. The reflection and transmission characteristics of the proposed AFSS unit cell are investigated. The simulation results show that the transmission and reflection bands of AFSS unit cell can be changed by setting diodes on and off. This new AFSS can be used to implement a sweeping radiation pattern at all azimuth angles. The antenna can sweep the entire azimuth plane in six steps and effectively operate over a bandwidth of more than 500 MHz.

articleTitle: An optimal-arranged metasurface for wideband RCS reduction
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a ultra-thin chessboard-like metasurface, whose arrangement is optimized to reduce both monostatic and bistatic radar cross-section (RCS) in a wide band. The optimized metasurface is formed by two kinds of lattice structures. The wideband monostatic RCS reduction is obtained by properly selecting the phase curve of both structures. Lattices of the metasurface are arranged in an optimized fashion, distributing the scattered energy to more directions and contributing to the great bistatic RCS reduction. The monostatic RCS reduction larger than 10dB has been obtained over more than 80% frequency bandwidth.

articleTitle: H-shaped aperture-fed bidirectional circularly polarized antenna using dual rotated patch
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A multilayer bidirectional circularly polarized antenna for underground communications is presented in this letter. The antenna consists of two slot-coupled back-to-back arranged rotated patches and a T-type strip feed-line. The H-shaped aperture is adopted to provide a favorable axial-ratio (AR) bandwidth. Identical left-hand circular polarization in the front and back of the radiating antenna is important in avoiding the undesired polarization mismatch for point-to-point connection. The proposed antenna combines the attractive features such as compact size, high aperture efficiency, as well as easiness of manufacture. Simulated results show that the antenna achieves a - 10 dB impedance bandwidth of more than 26% and a 3-dB AR bandwidth of 9% with a peak gain of 5.7 dBic.

articleTitle: Research on superdirectivity circular array of Koch fractal element
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The small physical size is a significant in the antenna design. Fractal geometry provides a good method for achieving the desired miniaturization performance. Therefore, apply 3rd Koch iteration technology to design miniaturization dipole element, and the operation frequency is 500MHz. Further, using the fractal antenna element to form uniform 5-element circular array, which is based on superdirective theory. The simulation and optimization have been carried out using FEKO software. The simulation results show that the directivity of designed model can realize 9.13dBi, which provides a good performance than conventional line array.

articleTitle: Design of broadband rectifying circuit by using five-sectional impedance matching network
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This work presents a novel study on the design of broadband rectifying circuit. Five-sectional impedance matching network is employed to obtain high conversion efficiencies of Radio frequency (RF) to Direct current (DC) in wideband. The Five-sectional impedance matching network consists of three transmission lines, an open-circuited stub and a short-circuited stub. As a consequence, the rectifying circuit has good performances from 1.7GHz to 2.7GHz. The rectifying circuit is successfully realized in theory and verified by full wave EM simulation, and simulated frequency response results show that the RF-DC conversion efficiencies of 46% and 45% are obtained at 1.8GHz and 2.4GHz. In addition, the designed rectifying circuit can be used for a variety of wireless charging systems.

articleTitle: Application of ADS-B for unmanned aerial systems: Case study and practical approach
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The National Airspace System (NAS) has experienced rapid growth in unmanned aircraft system (UAS) use and demand for airspace access. Expanding UAS military and civilian applications result in increasing demand for NAS access. It is driving the need for researches on UAS operations and air traffic management in a safe and effective manner. The ability for an unmanned aircraft to “sense and avoid” is the primary and pressing technical challenge. Sense and Avoid Systems (SAAS) have been perceived as potential solution for conflict detection and air traffic collisions avoidance, but the technical implementations for UAS have been far from satisfaction. One possible method for the SAAS to continuously localize surrounding aircraft and obtain traffic information necessary for integrating UAS may be through Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B). It is one of the most potential tracking technologies in Next Generation Air Transportation System (NextGen) to improve situational awareness for pilots. This paper examines the use of ADS-B system in future SAAS, possible implementations for UAS towards infrastructures, data link communication capabilities and satellite communication abilities. The technical challenges and safety concerns associated with UAS integration are presented. Finally, a practical approach of ADS-B unit for UAS based on soft defined radio in support with satellite relay and dynamic data link switch is discussed and developed.

articleTitle: A solar powered UHF transponder for wildlife and low light applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Autonomous solar powered transponders or wireless sensor nodes operate well in high sun irradiation whereas in low light conditions the efficiency of the solar cell decreases and full operation is not guaranteed any longer. This is likely to happen in wildlife scenarios particularly in shaded areas or in indoor environments. The presented transponder concept is designed to face exactly these challenging applications. This article describes the characteristic figures that have been evaluated for various different sending intervals of the transponder. The degree of efficiency for the harvested energy is optimized by using an optimum adapted maximum power point for the solar cell and thereby vastly improving the sensitivity of the system. This allows for a single-digit start-up time within minutes in low light conditions and accomplishes operation in lowest light conditions. Therefore, this transponder concept can also be applied in smart industrial indoor environments or any other low light condition scenario.

articleTitle: A compact 4 × 4 dual band-notched UWB MIMO antenna with high isolation
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A compact 4 × 4 ultra-wideband (UWB) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is presented in this paper. The proposed UWB MIMO antenna has dual band-notched characteristic in WIMAX (3.3 – 3.8 GHz) and WLAN (5.15 – 5.35 GHz and 5.725 – 5.825 GHz) frequency with a total dimension of 56 mm × 56 mm × 0.8 mm. Meanwhile it consists of four patch antenna connected with orthogonal protruded ground parts respectively. To achieve band rejection of WIMAX frequency, a λ/4 I-shaped open slot is etched in each radiating patch. Etching a λ/2 C-shaped slot into each patch obtains notched band in WLAN frequency similarly. To meet high isolation better than 20 dB for frequency under 4.2 GHz, four rectangular and four staircase-shaped stubs are added to ground parts of the proposed UWB MIMO antenna. The simulation results show that the proposed UWB MIMO antenna operates from 3.2 to 10.7 GHz with good performance of |S11| ≤ −10 dB and high isolation of |S21| ≤ −20 dB. Therefore the proposed UWB MIMO antenna can be utilized as a promising candidate for UWB MIMO systems.

articleTitle: Null steering using low profile weights for base station antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes null steering using weights which are consisted of only two low profile components, attenuator and phase shifter. The attenuator and phase shifter are calculated based on the antenna that is currently utilized at base station. Then, attenuator and phase shifter are fabricated and measured. Next, base station antenna pattern with weights is simulated to confirm it can steer mainbeam in desired direction and placing null in interference directions. Afterward, the performances of the system in terms of SINR and channel capacity are revealed. The result can confirm that the proposed weights can be adopted to use in the antenna that is currently used at base station to enhance the performance of the system.

articleTitle: A near-field radiation source localization method based on passive synthetic arrays using single channel receiver
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A new method of near-field radiation source localization, which is based on passive synthetic array (PSA) using single channel receiver, is proposed in this paper. Based on the concept of PSA in combination with the spatial spectrum estimation, the paper uses a revised multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm to estimate the distance and angle of interfering sources, and also proposes a method of Hilbert phase extraction based on the EMI receiver to locate near-field radiation sources. The derived array model is structurally simpler than the conventional array model, and solves the problem of multi-channel amplitude-phase inconsistency. It also avoids the problem that the model size is too big to use in the near-field situation. The feasibility of this method is demonstrated with simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Design of X-band GaAs power amplifier
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a design of X-band GaAs power amplifier with the technology of external impedance matching. According to the scattering parameter (S parameter) of field effect tube (FET) provided by manufacturer, the matching circuit and direct current (DC) bias circuit of power amplifier can be designed. The advantage of this method is that the work frequency, efficiency, gain and output power can be designed according to the actual situation by engineers autonomously. In addition, the method has the advantages of low cost and high efficiency. Simulation and practical measured data show that, when the center frequency is 8.2 GHz, the small signal gain is 8.1 dB, and the maximum output power is 31.25 dBm and the maximum power added efficiency (PAE) is 33.62 %.

articleTitle: Simulation study of plasma antenna reconfigurable performance
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Plasma antenna is a kind of reconfigurable antenna, its antenna frequency and radiation pattern can both be quickly changed by altering the input ionizing power and turning on certain antenna array elements. This article introduce our HFSS analysis method in the study of plasma antenna and array. As a preliminary study, we simulate the reconfigurable performance of a two elements plasma antenna array.

articleTitle: Reaserch on Au/Sn solder of microstrip in aluminium cavity
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Eutectic is an important technology of microelectronics assembly. It has a vital effect in microwave circuit. In this article, the briefly principle of eutectic is discussed firstly, then the factors that the Au thickness of the substrate metallization, the pressure on the substrate and sintering process curve analysis were studied in the eutectic progress. The experiment shows that when the Au thickness of the substrate metallization is about 3μm, a high quality of welding can be achieved in 340°C using 60s by vacuum eutectic curve. The results shows that welding on the Al substrate has a low welding void raio, the penetration rate is up to 95% and the shear strength of samples can meet the requirement of GJB548B-2005. Finally, the welding mechanization was invested in this article.

articleTitle: A non-invasive permittivity measurement based on split-ring resonators at microwave frequencies
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the microstrip-line-excited spilt-ring resonators to the permittivity measurement at microwave frequencies. The samples with specified thickness are placed on a well designed sensor, so that relatively large frequency offsets due to the samples can be detected to retrieve the permittivity. Analysis and experimental measurements validate that by applying this method, permittivity can be linearly retrieved from the measured frequency offsets. The measurement setup can be conveniently calibrated with a given sample with known permittivity.

articleTitle: Design of a microstrip fed spade shape planar monopole antenna for UWB applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a microstrip fed spade shape planar monopole antenna for ultra wideband (UWB) applications is presented. Modified shapes of the lower edge of spade shape patch and the upper edge of ground plane are optimized. The experiment and simulation are well agreement. The proposed antenna provide broadband impedance matching, appropriate gain and stable radiation patterns over its operating bandwidth from 2.8 GHz to 10.95 GHz for a 10 dB return loss and can be used in wireless UWB applications.

articleTitle: Modeling on electromagnetic susceptibility of operational amplifier OPA694
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the susceptibility prediction of integrated circuits against the conducted interference coupled on their power supply pins. An integrated operational amplifier OPA694 is studied as a first case. The integrated circuit electromagnetic (ICEM) model is used to describe the inner power distribution network of OPA694 by theoretical study and experimental measurement. A curve fitting method is proposed to obtain the ICEM model parameters from different kinds of measurements without knowing the precise inner physical structure information of OPA694. Then the direct power injection (DPI) experimental test is conducted to measure the susceptibility of OPA694 to conducted sine-wave noise. And from the immunity measurement, a common simulation susceptibility criterion is obtained. Finally the whole simulation model of DPI setup including the ICEM model of OPA694 is established to predict its susceptibility and the model is perfectly verified in a 200MHz frequency range.

articleTitle: 28-GHz path-loss measurement and modeling in indoor environments
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Channel measurements and path-loss modelling for typical indoor environments at 28-GHz band, in both line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight scenarios, are conducted. An automatic measurement system is designed and used, with multiple combinations of steerable transmit and receive antennas at both azimuth and elevation planes. Based on the measured data, the received signal is combined in plural, in azimuth and elevation plane, at both transmit and receive sides. Therefore the influence caused by the radiation pattern could be offset. Then, the path-loss is modeled as the product of a distance dependent term, and the standard deviation of shadow is also discussed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering of an E-polarized wave by a slotted semi-elliptical channel truncated by a metal plane
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A slotted semi-elliptical trench is flush-mounted under a metal plane, and is truncated perpendicularly by another metal plane. The scattered field due to a plane wave obliquely incident on this metallic structure is determined exactly, in the phasor domain.

articleTitle: A dual-band planar quasi-Yagi antenna with double-dipole driver
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A quasi-Yagi antenna with dual-band performance is presented. The proposed antenna consists of a printed double-dipole driver element fed by a 50 ohm coaxial line, two co-planar dipole directors and two reflectors. Different from the other quasi-Yagi antennas, this design employs a new driver element, which helps to obtain a dual-band functionality. The proposed antenna operates at 2.4-, 5.2-, and 5.8 GHz industrial, scientific and medical (ISM) band. It is printed on a dielectric substrate of thickness 0.8 mm and relative permittivity 4.4. The size of the antenna is 33×52 mm2.

articleTitle: Ultra-broadband metamaterial absorber using slotted metal loops with multi-layers and its ECM analysis
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: An ultra-thin and broadband absorber which consists of periodic rings with gaps is proposed in this paper. The periodic rings are printed on the middle metallic layers in a four-layer substrate of total thickness is only 3.4mm. Simulation results, which are gotten by using FEM, show that the absorption is higher than 90% cover the frequencies range from 8.4GHz to 23.6GHz. The measurement results of the absorption agree with simulated ones very well. We also give the Equivalent Circuit Model(ECM) of the absorber structure.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable OTA chamber: A new paradigm for testing of MIMO wireless devices
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Over-the-air testing (OTA) of wireless devices in realistic but repeatable environments is typically performed using either an expensive multi-antenna OTA chamber that provides a high level of multipath control or a low-cost mode-stirred reverberation chamber that offers limited multipath control. We introduce a reconfigurable OTA chamber whose walls are lined with antennas, a few of which may be attached to a channel emulator and the balance of which are connected to reconfigurable impedances. Initial simulations and measurements with this topology demonstrate that through control of the impedances and the port excitations, the chamber offers significant control over the achieved fading distribution, spatial correlation, and power angular spectrum at the device under test.

articleTitle: A novel moving average method of vehicle detection in the FMCW radar using antennas with different beamwidths at K-band
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a moving average method (MAM) applied to the target detection in the FMCW (frequency modulated continuous waves) radar, which uses array antennas with different characteristics of radiation beam-with at K-band. The MAM may smooth out the short-term fluctuation in the system responses by using the received data in time series It is a statistics method to analyze the data points by creating a series of data averaged from different subsets of the full data set. It is especially useful for the radar system with over-narrowed radiation beamwidth of antennas[1]. In this paper, the FMCW radar is operated at 24.125 GHz with 250 MHz bandwidth, and implements a linear frequency modulation (LFM) for TX/RX with 1mW in TX power. The output responses are the peak values of signals after being processed by the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and MAM. The experimental results are presented to show the reflection responses of a vehicle within the FMCW radar coverage range.

articleTitle: Analysis of absorptive and transmissive radome
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper analyzes the influence of geometric dimensions of absorptive/transmissive radome to its performance based on equivalent circuit theory. When the impedance of free space matches the impedance of absorber, no wave would be reflected and most energy would be absorbed. The absorptive/transmissiveradome is consisted by aperture frequency selective surface(FSS), substrate and absorptive FSS. Aperture FSS decides the pass band of radome and resistive FSS and thickness of substrate has great influence on the absorptive band. Conclusions obtained by equivalent circuit theory were verified in HFSS.

articleTitle: Design and performance study of AOS multi point communication system in spatial noise environment
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In the current AOS communication system model, internal information processing of communication system is the emphasis of the research and the information processing and anti-interference performance of AOS communication system is seldom considered in the spatial noise environment. In this paper, we establish a spatial noise environment model based on the current AOS communication system model, considering the type of transmission source. Then the AOS communication system is simulated by VC++ and MATLAB simulation software, in this process, spatial noise of information transmission process is simulated. The anti-interference performance of the system can be analyzed from the simulation results. The results provide a theoretical basis and reference for AOS communication system design.

articleTitle: Characteristics of the electromagnetic radiation emission from coaxial cable of a type inverter
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic radiation emission from cable [1] is one of the most important factors to cause electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) problem for the inverter, which may directly lead to the performance degradation or failing to work normally for the device. In this paper, the characteristics of the electromagnetic radiation emission from coaxial cable will be researched by means of simulation and calculation. An example of a type inverter is introduced at last.

articleTitle: Study on effect of earthing resistance on EMU radiation emission
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This article is based on the existing national standard and discussed the standard test method and standard process. It was proposed that EMU traction return current could generate differential-mode radiation between the vehicle body and the rails, and an equivalent model was established. Based on the test, the EMU radiation emission was discussed in the static low-frequency (9KHz-11MHz) magnetic field with different earthing resistances. Tests show that the 50 milliohms earthing resistance between the EMU vehicle body and the rails can improve the EMU static radiation emission characteristic in low-frequency magnetic fields. An improving plan for the EMC design of high-speed EMU on suppressing the EMU electromagnetic radiation was provided.

articleTitle: Research on harmonic characteristics of traction transformers and traction converters
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Harmonics of traction system could affect the normal operation of the track circuit in high speed railway. In order to understand the harmonic fully and to reduce the harm from harmonic, this paper analyzes the harmonic characteristics of the traction transformers and traction converters separately in theory. Furthermore, the harmonic characteristics are shown by simulation and on site test data.

articleTitle: Simulation of impact of sea clutter to radar detecting performance
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper builds a electromagnetic scatter model of sea clutter. Many sea elements, such as multipath effect, wind velocity and wind direction, are considered in this model. RCS of sea clutter for different sea state can be computed through this model. In the background of sea clutter, the performance of ship based radar is simulated in this paper. According to simulation data, the conclusion of the impact of sea clutter is drawn.

articleTitle: A synthesis method for substrate integrated coaxial line with different dielectric layers
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A new calculation method for the equivalent width of the substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL) with two dielectric substrate layers, the same height and different permittivity is proposed in this paper. The SICL is approximately modeled as a rectangular coaxial line (RCL) of the same characteristic impedance using the equivalent capacitance theory, with equivalent width weff. Lastly, the proposed calculation method was proved effectively by simulation results.

articleTitle: A broadband and miniaturized V-band passive MMIC frequency doubler
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The paper presents a wideband V-band passive MMIC frequency doubler. It consists of input match circuit, two balanced diodes and a passive balun. The input match circuit is mainly consisted of parallel capacitor to ground, which could be taken as input match. Two balanced diodes are constructed by HEMT (High Electron Mobility Transistor) where drain and source have been short-circuited. The passive balun adopts a novel, but very simple structure, which makes two-way signals attain 180° phase difference in a very wide frequency range. The doubler is simulated in ADS and is fabricated in the OMMIC process. The measurement results show that this doubler has relatively low conversion loss, about from 10dB to 13dB when input power level is bigger than 10dBm. The doubler also has favorable suppression over 1/2 and 3/2 spurs, which are better than 20dB, from 40GHz to 75GHz output frequencies. In addition, the doubler occupies little area, only 0.6mm2, and so saves much cost.

articleTitle: Design of a novel single-feed antenna for global positioning system
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a circularly polarized microstrip antenna for global positioning system (GPS). This single-feed and single-layer antenna works at the L1 (1559-1615MHZ) frequency band for civil use of GPS. There are two pairs of symmetric rectangular slots and circular slots in the diagonal directions respectively. The right-handed circular polarization (RHCP) is obtained by using the slight difference between the rectangular and circular slots. Four E-shaped shots are embedded on the ground plane to improve the antenna gain. The results show that the antenna gain has increased some 0.83dB. The -10dB impendence bandwidth is 39.3MHz and the 3dB axial ratio is 14.9MHz. It is obvious that this antenna can be used in GPS.

articleTitle: A novel broadband low loss millimeterwave power combiner
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel four-way millimeter wave power combiner based on waveguide power-combining circuit has been presented and investigated. The waveguide power combiner was achieved with the improved E-plane T-junction structure and the waveguide-to-microstrip transition structure. The corner cut and impendence transformer were placed in the T-junction waveguide to improve the port matching. The structure has advantages of easy fabrication, low loss and a wide operation band of 31.8%. The structure is simulated and optimized at W band by using Ansoft-HFSS. The combiner has demonstrated operation over a broadband of 75 GHz to 110 GHz with more than 9.2 dB return loss and less than 2.1 dB insertion loss. The simulated results illustrate very good match to the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Compact microstrip triangular patch antenna with meandered ground plane for GPS and CNSS applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Novel design of triangular patch antenna for GPS (Global Positioning System) and CNSS (Compass Navigation Satellite System) applications is presented. The proposed printed compact antenna has total size of 40×30 mm2 and consists of triangular patch fed by microstrip line. Open end slits pattern in ground plane of the proposed antenna is used for dual band operation. The antenna covers two bands of GPS applications L1 (1.57 GHz) and L2 (1.245 GHz) along with CNSS. Impedance bandwidth of 80 MHz is achieved at L2 and 110 MHz at L1 band with reasonable gain. Measured return loss and simulated radiation patterns of the antenna in different planes are shown in this paper.

articleTitle: The development of novel coaxial tester on electromagnetic shielding effectiveness measurement
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A novel coaxial tester based on the ASTM D4935-2010 standard for shielding effectiveness (SE) measurement of electromagnetic shielding materials in the frequency range from 30 MHz to 6 GHz was proposed in this paper. The critical aspects of different metal materials for the novel tester were discussed. The results of the study demonstrated that Return Loss(RL) parameter and resonance peaks below the cutoff frequency of the tester are dependent on option of materials.

articleTitle: Design of low-frequency Artificial Magnetic Conductor with interleaved gap and lumped elements
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: AMC (Artificial Magnetic Conductors) is an important part in the research about artificial electromagnetic materials. Currently, the main two trends in AMC is miniaturization and low-frequency design, especially the latter, which can help applying AMC into wireless communication antennas. This paper discusses some kinds of low-frequency AMC structure, with interleaved gap and lumped elements as key factors, and the lowest working frequency of AMC achieved is 165MHz, which can offer ideas for relating work in future.

articleTitle: Design and experimental verification of active RF front-end limiter with high isolation degree and nanoseconds response time
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Present RF front-end limiters were widely used to prevent physical damage to low noise amplifier or mixer circuits in the environment of HIRF and EMP radiation. As the limiters were generally designed on the base of passive PIN diode circuits, their output limited power was greater than 10 dBm, which could result in saturation of LNA and degradation of the receiver channel. In this paper, the design methods and experimental verification of a kind of RF front-end active limiter module with ultra-low limited output power were presented. The module consisted of a high power limiting module, an active control module and a low power limiting module, and it featured rather high isolation degree and short response time compared with commonly utilized passive PIN diode limiters.

articleTitle: Design of two-layer substrate integrated waveguide slot array antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Based on the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology, a two-layer slot array working at Ka band is designed by transferring the conventional waveguide resonant slot array antenna to the substrate integrated waveguide structure., which fed by standard metallic waveguide. The integration of the slotted-waveguide array with the feeding network is an important goal in the design process. Reduced size of the antenna can be obtained using multilayered substrates, the power divider can be integrated in different layers at the bottom of the slot array antenna by coupling inclined slots. with the characters of small, light weight, simple framework, it can be easy for produce.

articleTitle: Two types of Antenna optimizing design for EMP simulator
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: EMP Simulators are important installations to implement HEMP effect and adaptability validation test for electronic equipments and systems. Horizontal dipole and headstand cone are two types of HEMP Simulator Antenna, which radiate horizontal and vertical polarization pulse electric field separatly. Radiation field distribution of arc horizontal dipoles with different bend radius and conic monopoles with different slope angle are simulated in this paper, and an optimized project of simulator antenna is investigated to improve test area peak field strength or uniformity.

articleTitle: An original Vivaldi antenna for 1–8GHz wideband application
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A tapered slot Vivaldi antenna, which is fed by a microstrip-slot balun for 1–8GHz Wideband application is presented. The measured bandwidth of the proposed antenna for |S11| ≤−10 dB spans 0.9GHz to 9.6 GHz. The endfire radiation patterns in the x−y and y−z plane are obtained through the operating band from 0.9GHz to 5.8GHz. The antenna peak gain is 6.3 dB and measured gain is larger than 3.15 dB from 0.9GHz to 6GHz, however, the gain has a sharp decline at 8GHz. The structure and parameters of the Vivaldi antenna is designed and simulated.

articleTitle: A method about antenna layout optimization on particle swarm optimization
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Isolation between antennas is a key factor on the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) about aircraft. The optimization about antenna layout on airborne is a main method to solve the isolations problem. However, it is hard to find a compromising point to optimize antenna layout. Because when the position of antenna A is adjusted to optimize isolation with antenna B, it also affects isolation with other antennas. To solve above problem, a method about antenna layout optimization is proposed in this paper that FEKO7.0 is called by MATLAB based on the particle swarm optimization (PSO), which can optimize antenna layout on airborne. The PSO is realized, so that the optimal parameters can be adjusted. To consider the antennas working at different frequency bands at the same time, the “Less Design Rate” method is introduced to set the objective function of PSO. Above all, the method can improve optimal speed on the premise of ensuring the optimal effect. The accuracy of the method can be verified by dipole antennas.

articleTitle: Research on electromagnetic interference between power cables and shielded twisted-pair bundles
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: It often brings electromagnetic compatibility problems when dense and complex cables lay in modern ship cabin. This paper tries to analyze the electromagnetic interference between power cable and shielded twisted-pair bundle with the transmission line theory and shielding theory. We take an experiment in the shielded room on the electromagnetic interference between the power cable and shielded twisted-pair bundle. The results showed that the electromagnetic interference is relatively low when both ends of the external shield was grounded, and it would be the highest when only the non-tested end was grounded. We should take the ground surface current into consideration and keep all the ground is in same position. in addition, the shield should be grounded well.

articleTitle: Capacity analysis of OAM multiplexing system for radio communications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The orbital angular momentum (OAM) applied to wireless communication has been verified feasibly. To achieve better performance, the influence of both OAM modes at the transmitting side and antenna configurations at the receiving side on system capacities is researched by exploiting the method of singular value decomposition (SVD). It is found finally that, non-uniform receiving array configuration can also achieve better results. Moreover, the performance may be poorer with more receiving antennas, due to the emergence of correlation. Besides, to further improve the performance, optimizing power allocation should be considered.

articleTitle: Design of a Ka band dual mode filter based on LTCC technology
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A Ka band dual mode filter based on LTCC technology is designed in this paper. This filter is realized by using cylindrical cavity with pin mode. The filter is a four order cross coupled filter with a pair of transmission zeros, its center frequency is 35 GHz and the bandwidth is 1GHz. EM simulator HFSS is employed in determining and optimizing the physical dimension of the filter. The simulation results show that the insertion loss of the filter is less than 2.6 dB, and the return loss is better than 20dB, which can meet the requirements of the design well.

articleTitle: Direction of arrival estimation of nonstationary signal based on time-frequency music
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Spatial time-frequency distributions (STFDs) matrices has been introduced to deal with non-stationary source signals. This paper discusses how to achieve high-precision direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation with STFD matrices. Also we try our best to reduce the amount of calculation. In order to reduce the calculation cost in practice, a new method based on single time-frequency point to estimate DOA of source signals is proposed in this paper. This method accelerates the calculation speed and lowers the computation time in a large part. These conclusions are verified by simulation experiments based on MATLAB.

articleTitle: Design, fabricate and test of a new kind of high power microwave directional coupler
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a new kind of high power microwave directional coupler operating at 1.72GHz to 2.61GHz is presented. To get a directional coupler with very weak coupling but high power capacity, a two-stage coupling strategy is proposed. Multi-holes coupling structure is used for the first coupling stage, and double cross-aperture is used for the second coupling stage. The coupling factor's variation trends of these coupling structures can be designed to be opposite. Then a very flat frequency response will be got. The two-stage directional coupler is designed and fabricated. The measurement results show that this directional coupler has a good performance. The deviation of the coupling is smaller than 0.8dB, and this directional coupler can work normally when a 2MW pulse microwave power put in it. The potential peak power capacity of this directional coupler could be much higher.

articleTitle: Parallel higher-order method of moments using 100K CPU cores
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The use of higher-order basis functions (HOBs) reduces the number of unknowns in method of moments (MoM) compared with the piecewise basis functions. To significantly improve the capability of MoM, a scalable parallel algorithm with a LU decomposition direct solver is extended to efficiently use more than 100K CPU cores on the world's fastest supercomputer, Tianhe-2. The proposed algorithm has the potential to solve large complex problems that were unattainable in the past by MoM. An airplane model with 671,777 unknowns is simulated to demonstrate the performance of the proposed algorithm, and the overall time is only about 20 minutes.

articleTitle: The study of 2.45 GHz atmospheric microwave plasma generator
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Atmospheric pressure microwave plasma has potential been wildly applied to the experiment and industry. But the equipment of the microwave plasma is not easy to control. In order to make it easier to control, we simulated three adjustable parts to figure their effects out. In this paper, we introduced the structure of the microwave plasma generator, and studied the effects of three parts of the structure by simulation, and measured by the Agilent vector network analyzer (VNA) E50618 10MHz-3GHz. From the simulation and the measurement result, we can get some rules and conclusions of the microwave plasma generator.

articleTitle: A new recursive filter based on the Gauss von Mises distribution
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Many state estimation or sensor fusion algorithms are based on traditional filtering techniques such as the Kalman filter, the extended Kalman filter (EKF) or the unscented Kalman filter(UKF). However, these approaches all make Gaussian assumptions, without taking into account the intrinsic structure of the underlying state space. In this paper, to properly perform estimations on a cylindrical manifold, Gauss von Mises(GVM) distribution model is employed, a new GVM parameter estimation method is presented, and a novel GVM filter(GVMF) is proposed. The effectiveness of the proposed GVMF is illustrated in a case study in motion estimation involving the tracking of an object in a three-dimensional state space. Results demonstrate that more accurate estimates can be achieved with the proposed GVMF in comparison to the traditional EKF.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of infrared photodetectors with Au gratings by FDFD method
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Quantum-well infrared photodetectors have been studied extensively due to their night vision, astronomy and environmental monitoring research in recent years. However, responsivity and detectivity are relatively low in these photodetectors without the Au gratings. Therefore, the Au grating will be employed on the surface of photodetector with periodic structure due to the principle of spoof plasmon resonance. The new design mainly aims to enhance the absorption in the QW active region based on the Au grating and can be numerically simulated by using finite-difference frequency-domain method. With optimal grating parameters, the absorption can be enhanced by hundreds of times compared with that in the reference structure without grating. The theoretical results provide the realistic organic infrared photodetectors with theoretical basis and technical support.

articleTitle: A ripple shaped and dielectric loaded water-drop antenna for ground penetrating radar
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A innovative water-drop antenna with ripple shaped and dielectric loaded on the surface of the water-drop is presented for ground penetrating radar. The reflector plate is utilized behind the proposed antenna to enhance the radiation directivity. Finally, this design working at 400 MHz center frequency achieves 20% relative bandwidth approximately within S11<−10dB and VSWR<2. Likewise, the stable radiation pattern and higher gain more than 7 dB are obtained over the required frequency region. Also, the miniaturized structure is realized.

articleTitle: A new fast time domain physical optics algorithm based on analytic integral
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Based on the analytical integral method of PO algorithm, the analytical integral method of TDPO method is given in this paper, which can be applied to the case of differential Gauss pulse incidence. The computational efficiency of the TDPO algorithm is significantly improved by this method. Then, the idea of system transfer function is adopted, with this idea the time domain waveform of any kind of incidence can be obtained. Finally, several numerical examples are given. Numerical results show that the algorithm in this paper is accurate and effective.

articleTitle: Radiowave propagation loss measurement of different situated Knife-Edge problems and comparison with PO computing
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this article, an indoor radiowave propagation loss measurement environment which worked at 9.375 Ghz was built and a series of experiments about propagation loss of different situated Knife-Edge were implemented. The Knife-Edge position changes caused by horizontal length change and angle change were experimental studied respectively. The influence of Knife-Edge horizontal length and angle changes on propagation loss was presented. Finally, a comparison between experiment results and PO computing results was given.

articleTitle: Investigation on the design method of TEM transition
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The design method of TEM transition from circular section to rectangle section is presented. To achieve good transition two design principles are constructed. Firstly, the section shape between circle and rectangle section should change slowly. Secondly, impedance of transmission line with arbitrary section between circle and rectangle coaxial transmission line should be kept exactly same impedance. The VSWR computing result validate the method of TEM transition from circular section to rectangle section.

articleTitle: Conducted electromagnetic emission analysis for airborne full bridge AC/DC SMPS
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes an analytical method based on two ports network to analyze the conducted electromagnetic emission interference of typical airborne full bridge AC/DC Switch Mode Power Supply (SMPS) in tow modes, which are common mode and differential mode respectively. According to the analysis results, the SPICE circuit model of the SMPS is established. The model is simulated and obtained the time domain results. The results are processed by an algorithm that considered intermediate frequency bandwidth influence. The frequency domain calculated results are compared with the practical measurement data. The compare results verify the feasibility and reliability of the above methods.
