articleTitle: An efficient near-field measurement technique for predicting far-field monostatic RCS of targets
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: An efficient near-field measurement technique for predicting far-field monostatic RCS of targets is studied. In the case that the height of the target is sufficiently small so that the far-field criterion is satisfied in the vertical direction, the theory and algorithm of near-field to far-field transformation for this measurement technique are derived. With the perfect conductor cylinder as the target under test, the computer simulation of this measurement technique is performed. The calculation results show that the far-field monostatic RCS obtained by near-field to far-field transformation agrees with the far-field monostatic RCS calculated directly by EM simulation software FEKO very well, which proves the correctness and validity of this measurement technique.

articleTitle: Theoretical analysis for constitutive parameters of the periodic electric resonator metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: We begin with Maxwell's equations and put the thin electric resonance dielectric sheet equivalent into electric surface current. Using periodic boundary conditions and the principle of superposition, we can get the dispersion relation and Bloch impedance of periodic electric resonator metamaterials. Base on the dispersion relation and Bloch impedance, we can obtain the theoretical analytical expressions of Bloch constitutive parameters. Since we consider the impact of the magnetic anti-resonance, we find theoretical predictions match the retrieval results very well, which showed that the analytical expression derived in the paper is extremely effective.

articleTitle: Efficient evaluation of near-field PO scattering from PEC objects illuminated by arbitrary far-field sources
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Antennas radiation on electrically large objects is often encountered in computational electromagnetics. In this paper, we present an approximation strategy for the line integral reduction of arbitrary far-field source excitation. By approximating the arbitrary far-field source as different vector point sources for each sub-segment on the contour of the PO integral surface, the PO scattered field is cast in a line integral format. This algorithm permits a fast and accurate evaluation of the PO integral for arbitrary far-field source excitation. Compared with traditional line integral approach by expressing the incident wave as angular spectrum of plane waves, our method is simpler and more explicit. Numerical examples are presented to illustrate the exactness of the line integral representation.

articleTitle: Meshless-based multilevel fast multipole algorithm for solving volume integral equations with complex media
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) problems with complex media are formulated by volume integral equations (VIEs) in the integral equation approach. The VIEs are usually solved by the method of moments (MoM) with the Schaubert-Wilton-Glisson (SWG) basis function, but the solution requires high-quality conforming meshes, resulting in a high cost in geometric discretization. In this work, a point-matching meshless method is proposed to discretize the VIEs and it uses discrete points instead of meshes to represent an object domain. Also, the method chooses the current densities as the unknown functions to be solved so that the integral kernels are free of material parameters. For electrically large problems, we incorporate it with the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) to accelerate the solving process. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the method and good results have been observed.

articleTitle: Simulation of the response of mixer
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper founds a response model of the mixer. Three kinds of nonlinear elements are included in this model. The three nonlinear elements are negative gain element, switch element, and port coupling. This model is accurate to compute the response of the mixer. Adopting this model, this paper simulates the response of mixer, and draws the conclusion.

articleTitle: A multimode annular ring patch antenna for MIMO applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a multimode microstrip antenna consist of two annular ring patch antennas operating at its TM11 and TM21 modes respectively for four ports multiple input multiple output (MIMO) applications is investigated. Both the two parts are dual-polarized. The inner patch which has cross slot in the center is excited by coaxial probe and the outer ring is excited by a microstrip curved bend. Therefore four different radiation patterns are achieved. The antenna operates at 2.57 GHz and exhibits a mutual coupling between the four input ports less than −17dB in simulation and −16.5dB in measurement. The antenna is designed based on cavity model and verified by HFSS.

articleTitle: Analysis and validation of hybrid model for signal via structures in complex conditions
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A hybrid model is proposed for signal structures of PCBs and packages. The stack-up structure can be decomposed into several types of different sub-structures: microstrip line-via transition structure, via structure and strip line-via transition structure. In order to get good result, the strip line-via transmission structure is analyzed by the improved matrix-penciled moment method, vias are modeled by the intrinsic via circuit model , whereas the strip line-via transitions are described by modal decomposition. Finally microwave network cascade method is used for get the result of the complete structure. Full-wave solver HFSS have been used to validate the method and good agreements have been observed.

articleTitle: Design of an aperture coupled frequency selective surface
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Two methods has been proposed to improve frequency selective surfaces' cut-off of sidebands, that's, three-order characteristics and transmission zero characteristics. The three-order characteristics is achieved with the design of one-order resonant coupling aperture and the transmission zero characteristics with the design of two coupling channels between patch unit and intermediate aperture. Also, the frequency selective surface has been miniaturized to improve its angle stability, which is achieved by unit interdigitated methods. The above methods are all simulated and optimized with numerical simulation (finite-element method) and the final design characteristics are validated with experimental results.

articleTitle: Wireless communication for heavy haul railway tunnels based on directional antenna radiating same direction
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Radio-over-fiber (RoF) technology is a comparatively mature technology which can effectively improve the reliability and quality of service (QoS) in railway communication systems. As a coverage strategy of RoF in long heavy haul railway tunnels (more than 1 km), directional antenna radiating same direction is highly valued. Due to the handover mechanism changed, handover trigger probability and outage probability will be adopted to investigate its performance. Compared with the traditional model, this strategy, which deployed by a number of RAUs (remote antenna unit) using directional antenna in long tunnels, has its own advantages. It can be concluded that when using directional antenna radiating same direction, the trigger probability can almost reach 100% when entering the overlapping area and the outage probability is lower.

articleTitle: Incorporation of meshless scheme with contrast source inversion method for reconstructing dielectric objects
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Contrast source inversion method (CSIM) is one of robust methods for reconstructing dielectric objects by integral equation approach. The method requires an intensive calculation of volume integrals over imaging domain in the optimization of cost functional and the process is very tedious. In this work, we incorporate a novel meshless scheme with the CSIM to simplify the calculation of volume integrals so that the reconstruction can be accelerated. The meshless scheme changes the volume integrals into boundary integrals through the Green-Gauss theorem when the integrands are regularized by excluding a small cube enclosing the observation node in the imaging domain. Numerical examples for reconstructing two contacting dielectric spheres are presented to illustrate the inversion approach and good results have been obtained.

articleTitle: Prediction of shielding effectiveness of some complex structures on vehicle platform
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Shielding effectiveness of metallic enclosures with curved metallic objects on vehicle platform illuminated by an incident EMP is studied using hybrid FDTD method combined with a modified conformal technique. Some important factors including polarization direction of the incident wave, the incident angle of the exterior EMP, and different incident waveforms are investigated in detail for their effects on SE. Some valuable conclusions are brought forward. Some effective design issues are addressed so as to enhance the shielding performance of metallic enclosures.

articleTitle: Numeric study on EM-mechanical properties of an electromagnetic launcher
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic rail launcher has a wide range of applications. Inductive shunt device is usually paralleled with the rails of the launcher as an approach to limit muzzle arc by transferring armature current. The shunt parameters will significantly influence the rail current, armature velocity and device stress conditions, which also makes the physical process more complicated. In this paper a circuit-electromagnetic-mechanical coupled simulation model is developed to analyze the launching process. Based on this model, the influence of shunt impedance, armature resistance and capacitor energy are investigated numerically. Stress conditions and deformation of shunt are studied as well. Some launcher design suggestions are given according to the conclusion.

articleTitle: Three-frequency transceiver integrated microstrip antenna based on the harmonic measurement
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Based on harmonic measurement, the paper designs one transmitting two receiving triple frequency microstrip antenna respectively working at 2.4 GHz and 4.8 GHz, 7.2 GHz bands. The two high frequency antennas are placed side by side at the top of the low frequency bands antennas, which can realize low frequency bands antennas transmit electromagnetic wave and two high frequency antennas receive reflected wave.

articleTitle: Recent advance in anomalous modal behaviors of integrated guided structures for THz applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents the anomalous modal characteristics of the periodic substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and two-dimensional periodical perforated microstrip on the mesh ground. A Full-wave eigenvalue approach is proposed to extract the complex propagation constants, showing the additional leakage phenomena in the two guided-wave structures: the surface wave leakage occurs at the cutoff frequency of the rectangular waveguide section of the SIW; and a new form of electromagnetic leakage near and above the leaky-mode region.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of X-band substrate integrated waveguide Vivaldi array antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A substrate integrated waveguide Vivaldi array antenna is designed and analyzed. The array antenna is made of two Vivaldi structure radiation elements, and the antenna is fed by an equal power divider with substrate integrated waveguide technology. Each radiation element is index gradient antipodal structure are on both sides of substrate. The reflection coefficient of the array antenna is less than -10 dB from 8.6 GHz to 10 GHz. The gain of the array antenna is 10.3dB.

articleTitle: Application of curve fitting in EMS test of CRT display
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The video graphics array (VGA) interface is a standard interface for display. The exposed interconnection cables of VGA interface are often the introducers of electromagnetic interference (EMI). The test method of bulk current injection (BCI) was used in the electromagnetic susceptibility (EMS) of cathode ray tube (CRT) display for compute. In order to acquire the quantization relation between coupled signal of VGA interface cable and interference phenomena, the amplitude of coupled sinusoidal signal along the VGA interface cable needed to be picked up accurately. For the horizontal synchronization (HS) and vertical synchronization (VS) signals were digital ones, the coupled level was hard to acquire directly because of the effect of noise signal of theirselves. The method of curve fitting was introduced. Thus the amplitude and initial phase of the coupled sinusoidal signal could be gotten accurately, which provided solid foundation for quantizing the relation between coupled signal and interference phenomena.

articleTitle: Simulation research of the influence of different shape obstacles on the reflector antenna pattern
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In order to prevent the influence from obstacles on reflector antenna's performance, the installation environment of the reflector antenna is very strict. But on many platforms, the installation position of the reflector antenna cannot be easily changed. Therefore, it is necessary to know the effect of obstacle on the reflector antenna pattern. In this paper we have used simulation method to calculate the reflector antenna pattern influenced by metal obstacle, the obstacle is in two different shapes, cylindrical or prismatic. Then compared the influence extent of the obstacle's different shape on antenna gain and half power beam width (HPBW). Analysis shows that, on the condition of a given separation distance, the obstacle in the cylindrical shape has a relatively small influence effect on the reflector antenna gain and HPBW than the obstacle in the prismatic shape, the trend of gain loss curve of the cylinder obstacle is also relatively flat.

articleTitle: On the transient physics characteristics of PIN diode applied with microwave electromagnetic pulses
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In order to study the damage mechanism of PIN diode limiter induced by microwave pulse, basic semiconductor equations based on drift-diffusion model and two-dimensional finite element simulation method were employed to study PIN diode's electric field distribution, carrier concentration and lattice temperature changes under the effect of 2GHz high power microwave. Analysis showed that when it reaches the breakdown threshold, avalanche occurs first in region of the I layer close to the P-I junction. After the avalanche occurs, the electric field magnitude in the I layer declined rapidly. Peak-value electric field appeared separately at the P-I junction and the I-N junction, and these two positions is great point lattice temperature. In the positive half cycle of the microwave pulse, maximum temperature point appears in the center area of I layer. No matter breakdown caused by the negative pulse or injection of a large number of carriers caused by positive pulse, they are both likely to lead to the emergence of PIN diode's permanent physical damage.

articleTitle: Designing of new active frequency selective surface for HPM protection
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Conventional active frequency selective surfaces (AFSS) are designed with a DC biasing circuit to apply DC biasing voltage across active components. An innovative method to design AFSS is proposed in this paper to use an induced voltage across both ends of the surface loading components as the biasing signal to control FSS's transmission properties. The result from simulation proved that, a pass band exists on the AFSS at 3.5GHz when it is exposed to an electric field at a smaller intensity; at the electric field intensity (EFI) over 70 V/m, the insertion loss of the electromagnetic wave (EMW) increases at 3.5 GHz; in the case that the incident microwave's field intensity reaches 5000 V/m, the insertion loss is over 20 dB. This interesting phenomenon make the new AFSS has the ability of HPM protection, which mean that a pass band exists when EFI is weak enough, along with increasing incident field intensity, the pass-band finally turns into a stop-band because of the break though of the diodes.

articleTitle: Discretization of an square electromagneic cloak based on transformation optics
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Existing discrete electromagnetic cloaks are often limited to circular shape and always based on one dimensional discretization of radius variable in cylindrical coordinates. In this paper, we proposed a two dimensional (2D) discrete square invisible cloak which really does not require any continuous constitutive material parameters. The discrete square cloak consists of several homogeneous blocks, and they are discretized from the original transform medium whose material parameters are often continuous spatial functions of both x and y variables in Cartesian coordinates. With proper design of numbers of blocks, we demonstrated the scattering properties of the proposed cloaking structure through rigorous analysis of the scattered electromagnetic fields. The proposed cloaking structure could be possibly realized, therefore may lead to a practical path to an experimental demonstration of electromagnetic cloaking.

articleTitle: A novel single-layer dual-band FSS with angular stability for satellite application
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A novel single-layer dual-band FSS with angular stability is proposed in this letter. The proposed FSS is consist of simply a metallic patch with crooked slots and a thin dielectric substrate. The FSS functioning as a band pass filter for satellite application at 1.575GHz and 2.491GHz which are the operating bands of GPS(L1) and BeiDou Navigation Satellite System(BDS). The overall size of the FSS unit cell is 0.15λ×0.15λ where λ corresponds to the wavelength of the first resonant frequency. Moreover, the proposed FSS also exerts high angular stability and it responses the same for both TE and TM operation modes because of its inherently symmetry.

articleTitle: Time domain response analysis with equivalent circuit models for dipole antennas under EMP
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The dipole antennas are widely used for RF communication applications and usually provide a potential front-door path of coupling electromagnetic pulse (EMP). In this paper, the transient current response of dipoles exposed to EMP is calculated with an equivalent circuit based model, which consists of an equivalent pulse voltage source and an antenna equivalent circuit. A center-driven wire dipole and a normal mode helical antenna are utilized for validate the circuit models. The results from the circuit based models agree well with data obtained from full numerical solution of the actual antennas. They takes only a few seconds to calculate the transient response with circuit models, which could also be directly connected to RF front-end circuits of communication system for electromagnetic susceptibility assessment.

articleTitle: A design of diplexer with high isolation and out-of-band rejection
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a diplexer with high isolation and out-of-band rejection is proposed. In the working band 1.5 GHz to 3.0 GHz, two transmission bands with bandwidth 30 and 22 MHz center at 1.95 and 2.12 GHz separately are realized. In each single path, a special section which not directly connects to “T” structure and the terminal port to let signals coupling twice before transmitting to the terminal. For each passband, to improve the roll-off rate, two transmission zeros are designed and set near the passband edges. Better than -30 dB out-of-band rejection is fulfilled, while the isolation between two bands is below -28 dB.

articleTitle: Highly flexible metamaterial designs in sub-terahertz using MEMS technique
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, two different micron-scale negative refraction index metamaterials with fine flexibility are proposed. The proposed metamaterials are composed of “Quasi-S” structure and “H” structure respectively. Different from conventional metamaterials, the designs proposed in this paper apply to perpendicular incident waves. Both metamaterials are designed and optimized for sub-terahertz application. Both metamaterials can produce negative refraction index around 100GHz. Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) technique is adopted to fabricate the proposed metamaterials due to their micron dimension geometric scales. The fabricated metamaterial film shows excellent flexibility in practical use due to its light weight and pliability. The refraction index produced by Quasi-S structure and H structure are approximately −14 and −80 respectively. A horn antenna is used to examine the metamaterial's impacts on wave propagation around 100GHz. Antenna gain enhancement can be achieved (e.g. approximately 3.012dB at certain directions.)

articleTitle: A triple cylindrical cavity W-BAND filter implemented in substrate integrated waveguide(SIW)
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: During the past one decade, a great number of substrate integrated circuits have been developed. This letter reports on a 94G band-pass filter, firstly using a specific triple cylindrical cavity structure implemented in SIW which is designed in ANSYS High Frequency Structure Simulation(HFSS) software. A transformation was built to connect the filter to the other circuit elements for its utility. The structure depends on a technology called Printed Circuit board(PCB), which is cheap enough for mass production. The result shows that a band-pass W-band filter with high performance is successfully designed.

articleTitle: A novel energy aware uplink cooperative link resource allocation method in LTE-A networks
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Considering the demand on energy savings in future wireless networks, consumptions on cooperative links between different base stations becomes more and more critical with the rapid development of wireless communication systems. Coordinated Multi-Point Transmission/Reception (CoMP) gradually becomes popular due to the demand of higher transmission rate and more reliable Quality of Service (QoS), but the utilization of cooperative links will bring additional power consumption in signal processing and transmission in system cooperative link. In this paper, we propose a novel energy aware resource allocation scheme in cooperative links to reduce the energy consumption in system backhaul link. Considering the energy saving in cooperative uplink transmission scenario, we propose a novel energy aware resource allocation scheme to reduce energy consumption without losing system performance. First, we group different users in a sub-optimal way by analyzing the distance and the traffic load jointly, then we propose a multi-stage resource allocation scheme in system cooperative link by using the optimal multi-stage cooperative decoding scheme. By reducing the traffic load transmitted in system backhaul, the energy consumption in system backhaul will be reduced significantly. Simulation result indicates that, our proposed method could gain about 32% of the total energy consumption in system cooperative link and the influence to system performance is less than 2%, which could be omitted.

articleTitle: Deconvolution technique for spatial resolution enhancement of MWTS
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Deconvolution technique is used in vertical polarization channel brightness temperature data of Microwave thermometer of FY-3 satellite for improving the ground spatial resolution. This paper applies the technique to the simulation images of MWTS and compares the experiment results firstly. Then the real data of MWTS is resolved, the relative geometry of every data samples changes over the scan due to the conical scanning of the instrument. The changes are resolved through designing different point-spread- function for every data in the reconstruction technique. The technique is applied in the Greece region, results indicate that, with the deconvolution technique, it is feasible to enhance the spatial resolution of MWTS, islands and the coast line in the enhanced express more details than non-enhanced brightness temperature images.

articleTitle: Parameter estimation using nonlinear least square approach for Synthetic Aperture Radars
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A nonlinear least square approach is proposed to estimate Doppler parameters of Synthetic Aperture Radars (SAR). The estimator includes Doppler centroid and Doppler frequency rate. Radar echoes are modeled as an Auto Regress (AR) process. AR parameters can be estimated by using Yule Walker method. Power spectrum density of radar echoes is derived from AR parameters. Doppler centroid and Doppler frequency rate correspond to the peak and the width of the power spectrum density.

articleTitle: An uplink energy-saving cooperation and power control scheme in heterogeneous cellular networks
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: It is significantly important to reduce uplink energy consumption in order to prolong the battery lifetime of user equipment (UE). In this paper, an uplink energy-saving power control scheme is proposed based on Coordinated Multiple Points Reception (CoMP) in the heterogeneous cellular networks. The main idea of the proposed scheme is based on the tradeoff between the uplink transmission power and system throughput. Firstly, cooperative UE obtains the gain of throughput via CoMP. Then, an energy-saving power control strategy is adopted to reduce transmission power of CoMP UE on the premise that transmission throughput is guaranteed. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme can effectively reduce the UE's transmission power and obtain approximately 9% gain in energy efficiency (EE) compared to conventional non-cooperation uplink transmission scheme.

articleTitle: A directional dual-band rectangular inverted-F antenna with Eleven slots for WLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A directional dual-band rectangular inverted-F antenna for WLAN applications is presented in this paper. By using the so-called Eleven-slot, the dual-band operation is obtained. The antenna have been designed and simulated in CST Microwave Studio. The results show that the antenna can provide wider impedance bandwidth in the higher resonant frequency by extending the slots to outside of the edge of the patch. The simulated 10dB impedance bandwidth in the dual-band are about 260 MHz (2.23-2.49GHz) and 630 MHz (5.21-5.84GHz) at dual bands, respectively, making it capable of covering the dual WLAN bands. Good radiation performances and nearly constant in-band antenna directivities are observed as well.

articleTitle: The minimum protection distance of receiving earth station in L band in China
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The minimum protection distance of meteorological receiving earth station in L band is analyzed in this paper, beyond which the receiving earth station in the frequency band 2200–2300MHz (L band) will not be interfered by the 4G LTE terminals. The methods to use in determination of the minimum protection distance are based on the ITU-R Recommendation P.1546-5 and the simulation analysis tool Wrap with the current typical technical characteristics of LTE system and meteorological receiving earth station. Through the field measurements, it is found that the calculation results obtained by Wrap are more practical and very close to the measured data. Furthermore, the effect of lumped interference from the LTE terminals to the single receiving earth station is also discussed in this paper. Finally, the operational and compatibility constraints for the above two services are given to ensure them working normally.

Author Keywords: the minimum protection distance of meteorological receiving earth station

articleTitle: The comparison analysis of scattering from model on the lake to target on the sea
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The spectra of wind waves in lake Michigan was introduced for computing the electromagnetic scattering from the rough lake surface. In addition, the JONSWAP ocean spectrum is used in this article to generate numerical data for the scattering of random rough sea surface. The normalization RCS (NRCS) is computed as a function of the incidence angle. It is found that the NRCS of the scaled lake surface is equal to the data of the sea surface at near grazing incidence, while the discrepancy becomes increasingly greater than 3dB in other domain. It is also observed that the RCS of a given scaled target on the scaled lake surface is the same as the results of the corresponding target on the sea surface at the similar incident condition.

articleTitle: Simulation research on radar jammer's jamming to pulse compression radar
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In terms of working principle of pulse compression radar, a conclusion that frequency shift jamming has its advantage in jamming pulse compression radar is drawn based on the simulation analysis on pulse compression radar by noise jamming and frequency shift signal jamming of a radar jammer.

articleTitle: Trisection bandpass filter based on quarter-mode substrat integrated waveguide
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a microwave bandpass filter using a triplet configuration to realize cross coupling. A structure called quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW) is applied in these resonators to achieve the planar form. QMSIW is an isosceles right triangular microstrip patch loaded with an array of metallic via-holes along its hypotenuse which can be equivalent as an electric wall and the other two edges are equal to magnetic walls. The filter was simulated and fabricated at the center of 2.35GHz with a bandwidth of 330 MHz and good agreement was achieved between the simulated results and those measured.

articleTitle: Test sequence generating method of Cooperative Vehicle Infrastructure System based on support index
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: System Testing is a key technology of CVIS (Cooperative Vehicle Infrastructure System). A shortest test sequence generating approach in CVIS is proposed in this paper. The paper firstly analyzes the spatial-temporal state of vehicle and complexity of infrastructure in network. Then paper designs system features and test cases, and introduces the concept of support index of the test case to system feature. Then a shortest test sequences generating method and GA method are used to accelerate the convergence speed. The method in this paper provide theoretical basis and implementation guidance in CVIS testing.

articleTitle: A novel method to obtain diffraction field of phased array antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a method to calculate phased array antenna diffraction field which based on superposition principle and UTD. By calculating the diffraction field of each array element, the total diffracted field of the phased array antenna can be obtained. The method of this paper tries to avoid a full-wave split, so it can be quick and effective.

articleTitle: Applying risk assessment technique to electromagnetic compatibility analysis in Chinese High Speed Railway
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: There are more and more electromagnetic compatibility problems contributing to safety related errors, malfunctions and other failures in Chinese High Speed Railway. However, the classical EMC test and theory does not take into account risk analysis of EMC especially in safety critical systems. In order to help engineers to solve the EMC problems systematically, a method with risk assessment and management thinking is used in this paper. First the study proposes an EMC Risk Analysis Model (EMCRAM) based on the Hierarchical Holographic Modeling (HHM) with four levels. The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) is introduced to calculate the risk of EMC faults when the risk value of the indices is obtained with the method of EMC measurement and experts' knowledge and experience. To demonstrate the approach, it is validated by an application of railway signal system and the results show the EMC risk and vulnerability in the railway signal system.

articleTitle: Codebook design based on LBG algorithm for multi-antenna multi-stream systems
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Multi-antenna with multiple data streams is emerging as an enhanced technology to obtain the high capacity, such as in the IEEE802.11ac system and the future 802.11ax systems. Codebook-based precoding could be an efficient method to improve the performance of those systems. However, the existing multiple data stream precoding scheme in 802.11ac introduces too much feedback overhead which results in a lower effective transmission rate. What is more, most prior works on codebook design only focused on MIMO systems with a single data stream, which can not apply to multiple-antenna multiple-stream systems directly. In this paper, we analyze the precoding scheme in IEEE802.11ac system in detail, and then propose a low-cost codebook design method for multiple-antenna multiple-stream systems which is called matrix Linde-Buzo-Gray (LBG) algorithm. It modifies the generalized Lloyd vector quantization (VQ) algorithm by redefining the distance, centroid, and perturbation between matrices based on Grassmann manifold. Simulation results demonstrate that the modified method needs lower feedback cost and achieves smaller quantization error compared to the precoding scheme in the 802.11ac system.

articleTitle: Extraction of metamaterial parameters
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we present to retrieve the effective electromagnetic parameters of a metamaterial. In this retrieval method, calculated or measured scattering parameters are employed for plane wave incident obliquely on a metamaterial slab at different angles. We not only can extract the electric permittivity ε and the magnetic permeability μ from calculation of the scattering S-parameters, but also can retrieval the components of electromagnetic parameters, then we can get any material parameter distribution of the material.

articleTitle: The vector perturbation precoding for massive multiple-input multiple-output based on GMD
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we think about the massive multiple-input multiple-output system analysis of vector perturbation precoding based on channel matrix geometric mean decomposition employing the minimum mean square error criterion with instantaneous power constraints for broadcast channels. Our analysis assumes that the transmitter has the imperfect channel state information and the receivers are acquainted with a perfect channel-dependent transmit power normalization factor. We propose a descent method by iteration for searching the perturbation vector in the complex field. The performances of the devised precoding scheme with the large quantity of transmit antennas and single-antenna users are studied in respect to bit error rate analysis through simulations and the numerical results illustrate it appropriated for massive multiple-input multiple-output system both in terms of complexity and performance.

articleTitle: Joint estimation and compensation of frequency-selective I/Q imbalance using loop-back method in OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Analog front-ends for wide-band wireless communication systems exhibit frequency-selective inphase and quadrature (I/Q) imbalance due to asymmetry in devices and layouts. This imbalance leads to a significant degradation of the performance in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems. In this paper, using a loop-back method, a joint transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX) estimation and compensation algorithm is proposed to estimate and compensate frequency-selective I/Q imbalance. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively eliminate the influence of frequency-selective I/Q imbalance with a very low complexity.

articleTitle: Research on the electromagnetic protection of high voltage cables in high speed EMU of power frequency magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Aiming at protect passengers with portable pacemaker, it is of vital importance to meet the standard in the design of EMU. In this paper, based on the theory of high voltage cable and electromagnetic protection, the model of high voltage cable passing through the compartment is established to simulate the magnetic flux density of the environment around the cable. In view of the actual situation, using sine, harmonic and inrush current as excitation source of high voltage cable under power frequency magnetic field. The results show that, under these conditions the magnetic field of the high voltage cable cannot affect the normal operation of pacemaker and the length of wire which is without shielding layer should be reduced as much as possible.

articleTitle: A novel blind multi-antenna spectrum sensing scheme based on phase difference in frequency domain
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel multi-antenna spectrum sensing scheme utilizing phase difference between antennas in frequency domain is proposed. Different from other multi-antenna spectrum sensing schemes just combining signal information from every antenna, the proposed scheme attempts to make use of the information between different antennas with the help of multi-antenna technology. As no prior information of signals is required, the proposed scheme can be seen as a kind of blind sensing (BS) schemes. Its theoretical analysis as well as practical implementation is designed based on the least squares(LS) estimation. The simulation results suggest that the proposed scheme is capable of achieving a better performance even under the condition of moderately low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and small number of symbols.

articleTitle: Coexistence research on improved cognitive OFDM signal and primary user signal
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Active interference cancellation (AIC) is known to be an effective technique for reducing the out-of-band radiation (OBR) of OFDM spilling over the primary user (PU) protected band. In order to ensure the OBR of OFDM is to be minimized, the AIC models with non-cyclic prefix, adding cyclic prefix were deduced and the performance was compared through simulation, then an improved AIC scheme with both cyclic prefix and adding hanning window is compared for cognitive OFDM systems, obtaining significant improvements in terms of notch depth. Further, this paper carried out a novel research on the coexistence of the OFDM with proposed AIC scheme and the signals of discrete carrier signals in 230 MHz band, and then experimental measurements through SystemVue platform validate its effectiveness, which concludes the performance of improved algorithm. In addition, we can observe the bits error radio of primary user signals, which can demonstrate the coexistence of OFDM signal with improved active interference cancellation algorithm and the discrete carrier signal in 230MHz band.

articleTitle: The significance of linear non-uniform electromagnetic wave in object detection
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Based on the antenna radiation theory, the universality, detectability and main characteristics of linear non-uniform electromagnetic wave are analyzed. When an object is illuminated by a linear non-uniform electromagnetic wave, there exists special phenomenon, such as induced eddy current and so on. Meanwhile, the definition of scattering function illuminated by a linear non-uniform electromagnetic wave is given. Computed by the method of moment (MoM), it is shown that the scattering characteristic of a metallic plate illuminated by a non-uniform wave is totally different from that by a uniform plane wave, and the peak magnitude is even bigger, which sufficiently demonstrates the significance of linear non-uniform electromagnetic wave in material detection.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a compact planar ultra-wideband fractal antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A compact co-planar waveguide (CPW)-fed planar monopole antenna using the Cantor and Koch is presented. The design achieves a good input impedance match throughout 2-18 GHz. The using of Conter with Knoch structure is shown to extend the antenna's impedance bandwidth for ultra wideband (UWB) performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the antenna exhibits the desired VSWR level and radiation patterns across the entire UWB frequency range.

articleTitle: Research on vehicle onboard measurement system of traction harmonic current for analyzing interference on Track Circuit
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Track circuit is one of the critical system in Train Control System that detecting the location of the vehicles. The track circuit could be affected by the harmonic generated by AC drive system. In this paper, a harmonic current measurement and manage system including hardware and software for evaluating the influence on track circuit system according CLS/TS 50238 is developed, and experimental measurements with respect to the harmonic of the vehicle traction system are carried out in Chinese railway line. Thus, the proposed measurement system could measure the harmonic current and evaluate the impact of harmonic current on Track Circuit system when the train is running. By analyzing the experimental data, the compatibility conclusion between Electric Multiple Units and Track Circuit, the distribution of the traction harmonic current and the regulations between traction harmonic current with different vehicle operating conditions are discussed.

articleTitle: A new prediction method for propagation loss in VHF
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: There are always some errors based on nonlinear equation by choice different models in propagation loss prediction. A prediction method for propagation Loss in VHF based on BP neural network is proposed, and the model structure of BP network is designed. Then the propagation loss in VHF is predicted using the measured data of the different terrain. The results show that the prediction accuracy of the proposed method is better than the nonlinear equation method, and the proposed method can be applied to different terrains and landforms.

articleTitle: Simulation of electromagnetic interference from high speed connectors in complex enclosures
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The high-frequency signals going through high-speed connectors are dominant interference sources in communication enclosures. However, it is difficult to estimate their EMC influence with numerical simulation. In this paper, a mixed strategy is proposed to simplify the EMI simulation of complex communication equipment. Firstly, a background transmission loss is introduced and determined by tested Quality Factor with Reverberation Chamber Theory to approximately model the resonance of real equipment. Then, Superposition Principle of active excitation is adopted to simplify the simulation of multi-signal transmission with random time delay. Furthermore, instead of integrative simulation with connectors and enclosures, the equivalent near-field source emitted by connectors is abstracted based on Huygens' Principle, and a co-simulation is realized with near-field sources and enclosures. The proposed method can accurately model the resonance characteristic of practical equipment, simplify the numerical simulation and ease the superposition effect analysis of multiple input signals with random time delay.

articleTitle: Analysis of a new kind of quadruple folded substrate integrated waveguide filter with LTCC technology by wave concept iterative process
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The article presents an efficient method named wave concept iterative process(WCIP) for characterization of substrate integrated waveguide(SIW) structures in LTCC. Firstly, an extensible approach of the iterative method to study substrates with n layers is researched. The approach involves the mixed magnetic and electric filed equation technique and the multilayer contribution of wave concept iterative process, which involves S-parameters extraction technique based on a simple form of Matched Load Simulation, and then, Substrate integrated circuits are considered as an ensemble of conducting vias placed in a parallel-plate waveguide. Finally, A new kind of multilayer SIW filter in LTCC is analyzed using the iterative method. Numerical results obtained are compared with the HFSS results. A good agreement is achieved together with significant improvements both in computational time and memory requirements.

articleTitle: Dual-frequency broadband patch antenna with matched load and capacitive patch
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-frequency broadband patch antenna with matched load and capacitive patch is proposed for GSM/DCS application. It is based on common patch antenna. In order to achieve the 900/1800MHz dual-band performance and directional radiation, the matched load and capacitive patch are added into modified antenna. As simulated by HFSS13.0 software dual-frequency broadband is obtained. The impedance bandwidth are 90MHz and 200MHz respectively. The calculated results were confirmed by measurements on the prototype.

articleTitle: Design of shaped elliptical beam antenna based on NURBS
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A new design method of a low profile shaped antenna with an elliptical beam based on the Non-Uniform Rational B-Spline surface modeling is proposed. The curves of the main reflector and sub-reflector in the plane when φ=0° are calculated based on the radiation pattern of the feed horn and the selected aperture field distribution function of the main reflector by using a shaping method; Then shape the curves of the main reflector and sub-reflector in any φ plane; Finally, model the main reflector and sub-reflector surfaces by using the Non-Uniform Rational B-Spline surface modeling. The simulation results show that the efficiencies of the designed elliptical beam antenna are 62.28% and 65.45% at 12.5GHz and 14GHz, respectively, the antenna achieves the performances of low profile, low side-side and high efficiency.

articleTitle: Solution of EM problems using hybrid parallel MIC/CPU implementation of higher-order MoM
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A hybrid parallel MIC/CPU implementation of the higher-order Method of Moments (MoM) is presented to solve electromagnetic problems. The basic parallel framework of MIC/CPU cooperative computing is on the base of environment variable. To boost program performance asynchronous communication technology is used for implementing communication hiding. Numerical results are given for a microstrip array antenna with dielectric structures. A speedup of about 1.8 times is achieved over the parallel CPU implementation.

articleTitle: An improved physic-based model for via structures embedded in layered media
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an improved physics-based model is introduced for vias embedded in layered media between two parallel-plate pairs. The model is constituted by upper and lower-via-to-plane capacitances and equivalent impedance matrix of the parallel-plate cavity. The via-to-plate capacitance is extracted by Q3D and the parallel-plate impedance is calculated by using the cavity resonator method (CRM) as well as equivalent wave number. For the first time, this circuit model is presented in this paper for the issue of layered media, which is much simpler with sufficient accuracy up to 20GHz when compared with analytical method. The modelis validated with full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of an acoustic source localization system based on 4-element cross-array
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an acoustic source localization method based on 4-element cross-array is presented, and an acoustic source localization system is designed. Four acoustic sensors are employed to collect the acoustic source signal, after several steps as amplifying, processing, AD conversion, generalized cross-correlation function method is used to compute the time difference of the signal arrival to the four sensors, then the position of the acoustic source can be determined. Experiments show that our system can achieve good performance in both speed and accuracy. The acoustic source localization system can be incorporated into a motion estimation system with low cost inertial sensors to increase estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Influence of excitation to results of channel measurement in frequency domain
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Comparing channel measurement results between single tone excitation, simple multi tone excitation and realistic communicational multi tone excitation, the influence to uncertainty of channel measurement in frequency domain is experimentally investigated. Reverberation chamber is used for simulate the complicate wireless channel used in practical applications. Signal generator is connected to the vector network analyzer to improve the traditional measurement method in frequency domain to the complex excitation type. Measurements on a connector are arranged for the control group. The influence is analyzed by averages of repeated measurements, and discussed from the aspect of nonlinearity of wireless channel and theoretical measurement uncertainty.

articleTitle: Design of a W-band four-channel dual-polarization waveguide slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The W-band full-polarization radar detection system is in need of a new type of antenna feed with good performance. The waveguide slot array antenna, has the advantages of low profile, high radiation efficiency, easy access to high gain. It has been become the research emphasis in the field of millimeter wave detection. In order to satisfy the need of developing complete polarization radar detection system, a W-band four-channel dual-polarization waveguide slot antenna is designed. The results of the simulation and optimization tests show that, the antenna has outstanding technical characteristics in double polarization. The antenna gain is higher than 13dB, and the cross-polarization level lower than -34dB. The bandwidth below VSWR 1.5 is better than 2.8GHz. High isolation of over 50dB is achieved between different polarization input ports.

articleTitle: A frequency-independent method of truncated wedge incremental length diffraction coefficients for large complex polygonal surfaces
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: We propose a frequency-independent method based on the truncated wedge incremental length diffraction coefficients (TW-ILDC). Considering the decay of fringe-wave surface currents and the fact that the discontinuous edges of a triangular patch in large complex objects are often small, the truncated lengths of such edges are often slightly varied. Hence a fixed length can be taken from the engineering approximation to simplify the tracing procedure of TW-ILDC. Compared to the traditional ILDC method, the proposed approach has higher accuracy and gets rid of the non-removable singularities. The validation of the new method has been confirmed by numerical examples.

articleTitle: FEM simulations of NFC certification tests in mobile phone environment
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a study for modelizing a Near Field Communication (NFC) technology integrated in a mobile device. It also proposes a simulation environment to perform NFC certification tests in reader-writer mode with the EMVCo (Europay Mastercard Visa Contactless) reference PICC (Proximity Integrated Circuit Card) called EMV-TEST PICC. This study is divided in 2 main parts. The first part is focused on the device under test (DUT) model. It consists of the antenna model and the ferrite inclusion followed by the chip output impedance characterization and the matching circuit model. The second part deals with the environment test and its model. This includes the coupling effect model with the reference device and a mobile phone simplified model finally followed by the power transfer test as define in EMVCo certification norm. Obviously, each study step is validated by comparing the simulated results with measurement ones.

articleTitle: Accurate solution of combined field integral equation for electromagnetic scattering by composite bodies
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The Nyström method is used to solve for electromagnetic scattering by three-dimensional composite bodies based on combined field integral equation. In the method of moments solution, one may hesitate on how to represent the magnetic current density using an appropriate basis function if the electric current density is represented by Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) basis function. Using the RWG again, or n̂ × RWG and dual basis function to represent the magnetic current density will have an instability, fictitious charge, or high cost problem, respectively. The Nyström method is simpler to implement and it can also remove all those problems. Numerical examples show that the Nyström method is stable and efficient even for solving composite-body problems.

articleTitle: A method for electromagnetic radiation emission test in electromagnetic interference environment
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a new measurement method to immune noise for in-situ EMC tests is proposed. Different from the traditional virtual microwave chamber method based on adaptive noise cancellation technology, in the proposed method, technologies in array signal processing such as spatial spectrum estimation and adaptive beamforming are adopted to filter the ambient noise in space domain. This measurement method can effectively filter the co-channel noise and broadband noise, guaranteeing the distortion-free of radiation characteristics of equipment under test at the same time, which is proved by simulation.

articleTitle: Development of a temperature dependent dielectric constant measurement system
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a dielectric constant measurement system is presented, which can work at different temperatures from room temperature to 200°C. This system is developed based on the theory of NRW algorithm using coaxial line. The calibration standards are also designed for TRL calibration. Temperature distribution is analyzed and optimized carefully using ANSYS thermal analysis to make sure temperature is uniform on the test fixture and is safe enough to connect to Vector Network Analyzer (VNA). Frequency range of this system is from 1GHz to 18GHz.

articleTitle: A novel multiband absorber using treble-crescent-circuit resistive FSS
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A novel multiband absorber comprising single-layer resistive frequency selective surface (FSS) is proposed in this letter. The resistive FSS layer constructed from resistive/low-conductivity treble-circuits in the form of symmetric crescent moon is backed by a thin FR-4 material. Simulation results show that the proposed absorber can provide a triple-band absorber at frequency 11.7(GHz), 14.8(GHz) and 16.6(GHz) with absorption rate of 99.96%, 99.99% and 99.97%, respectively. The electric field distribution and influence of several significant parameters are then illustrated to analysis the absorption principle of the proposed absorber.

articleTitle: A novel strategy of the memory storage requirement in the FDTD/TDPO hybrid method
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel strategy of the memory storage requirement in a time-domain (TD) iterative hybrid technique, which combines the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method and the time-domain physical-optics (TDPO). A minimized time range requirement of the shared information for all the observation points is determined by the analysis of the causality of transient EM fields. This range requirement is only depend on the distance between the FDTD-region and the TDPO-region which allows less memory storage without reducing the computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of explicit FDTD in general arbitrary dispersive media
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The stability of FDTD method in arbitrary dispersion media is very import in many field. The von Neumann method combining with R-H criterion has been used to study the stability of the FDTD in arbitrary dispersion media, and the stability condition is proposed in this paper. Further, two examples is studied to show the validity of the stability of the proposed results. Because the arbitrary dispersion media is express as the general rational function, so the the stability condition in FDTD can easily be further extended to dual-negative media, even all kinds of dispersion medium.

articleTitle: Fast analysis of RFIC using multilevel Green's function interpolation method
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A full-wave multilevel Green's function interpolation method (MLGFIM) loop-tree (LP) algorithm based on PMCHWT integral equations is proposed for the fast analysis of EM system in RFIC. To overcome the low-frequency breakdown problem, the LP basis function is adopted to preserve both inductive and capacitive phenomena at very low frequency. PMCHWT integral equations can solve composite metallic and dielectric structures of RFIC with the surface discretization. With the fast algorithm MLGFIM, the computation time and memory are greatly reduced. A spiral inductor example demonstrates its accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on mutual coupling reduction between monopole antennas by using an E-shaped slot
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This article presents a novel structure for reducing mutual coupling between two diversity monopole antennas for WLAN 5.2/5.8 GHz applications. The structure has an E-shaped slot cut into the ground plane between the two monopoles. When the antenna spacing is 0 0.3λ0 (λ0-wavelength at 5.2GHz in the air), mutual coupling was -27.2dB at 5.2GHz and -31.1dB at 5.8GHz. The lowest mutual coupling of -31.9dB was achieved at 5.89GHz, which is 20.1dB improvement over the reference.

articleTitle: Determination method of immunity limits of electronic information equipment to high RF interference
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The determination method of immunity limits of electronic information equipment to high RF interference was given out. Aimed this method, the verification experiment is designed accordingly. By use of the method mentioned above, the immunity limits, sensitivity, and safety margin of electronic information equipment in high intensity RF electromagnetic environment (EME) may be determined in the present laboratory condition. The results can provide good reference for the research on the sensitive mechanisms of electronic information equipment and the limit meaning of GJB 151A/152A.

articleTitle: The research and design of Anti-radiation CMOS integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this essay, the characteristics and effects of CMOS integrated circuit on spacecraft is analyzed in the radiation environment. Based on the generation of radiation effect, the main anti-radiation design method is introduced in the CMOS integrated circuit area on designing and processing. In the outer space, there is prone to be CMOS semiconductor components of threshold voltage deviation, transdiode decreasing, substrate leakage current increasing and corner noise amplitude increasing in the CMOS integrated circuit. As a result, there are 2 measures proposed to protect against radiation of the integrated circuits. Anti-radiation CMOS integrated circuit and Anti-radiation Layout. Accordingly, testing result of anti-radiation LNA chips, the designed anti-radiation CMOS integrated circuits obtain the ideal effect in anti-radiation function.

articleTitle: A pre-amplifler circuit for VLC system
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a pre-amplifier circuit used in VLC system. By this circuit, the original low lever input can be amplified to make receive module much easier to get the information and increase MER/BER of the whole system. The amplified signal will be added on a DC voltage to light a LED. Design principles are illustrated separately into three parts. Measured result shows good agreement with simulated one. The amplifier factor and DC voltage are adjustable which can make a flexible usage in practical application.

articleTitle: Analysis and control of electromagnetic emission for ringing signal
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Ringing signal has widely existed in digital circuits like integrated circuits, DC-DC circuits, etc. The ringing appears in the roads due to the parasitic effect in high frequency or the impedance mismatch, and may cause logical errors in signal processing, as well as electromagnetic interference (EMI) to other devices. To have a deeper understanding of the electromagnetic characteristics, we analyze the generic causes of ringing, and formulate its mathematic time-domain expression. Based on the time-domain formulations, a study of spectrum characteristics for ringing is made with the aid of Fourier transform, trying to find out ring's electromagnetic features. We also study the square wave signal's properties in time-frequency domain. Comparisons between ringing and square wave have been made, in order to support the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) design of circuits.

articleTitle: Theoretical modeling method research of the antenna array element's radiation characteristics
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: In the research of phased array antenna's radiation antenna, the key point is the accurate characterization of the array element's radiation characteristic. In this paper, Huygens surface radiation theory was adopted to derive the radiation computing model of the printed dipole antenna array element. This model is different from the other wire dipole model because it has considered the array element's surface radiation characteristics. The numerical validation shows that the error of the model is less than 3dB.

articleTitle: Research of key technologies in microfabrication of terahertz thin film circuit on ultrathin quartz substrate
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Terahertz frequency multipliers and mixers hybrid integrated with discrete GaAs planar Schottky diode and ultra-thin quartz substrate circuit structure is a low-cost and reliable solution. Micro-nano fabrication technology of plane integrated circuit and micromachining technology of geometric division of plane array integrated circuit on ultrathin quartz substrate are mainly discussed. Both of them are realized by the process of temporary bonding and de-bonding. The results showed that these technologies were suitable for terahertz thin film circuits on ultrathin quartz substrate. It is concluded that microfabrication technologies will have broad application prospect to achieve key components in the terahertz band.

articleTitle: Effect study of power division and bandwidth of power divider on performance of super-heterodyne multi-channel millimeter-wave receiving system
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: Super-heterodyne multi-channel millimeter-wave receiving system usually shared with one local oscillator (LO) source by using power divider, and the uniformity of power division and the bandwidth of the power divider will affect the performance of system. In this paper, the effect such as LO power, frequency, on super-heterodyne mixer's performance of the receiving system are simulated and measured, and the minimum change of LO power and frequency is acquired for minimum influence on performance of mixer. The results provide the design reference and guidance of power division and bandwidth for power divider in receiving system.

articleTitle: Analysis of sinusoidal shaped microstrip bandstop filter by the static circuit parameters method
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: The full-wave and circuit method are combined to be utilized to analyze the performance of the sinusoidal shaped microstrip bandstop filter. The static distributed circuit parameters of the filter are extracted with the full-wave electromagnetic method, then used to construct the equivalent circuit. The frequency domain performance of the sinusoidal shaped microstrip bandstop filter are obtained with the input and characteristic impedance calculated from the equivalent circuit. Owing to better agreement between the S parameters obtained with static circuit parameters and the measured results, the effectiveness of the distributed circuit parameters applied to predict the performance of microstrip filter is verified.

articleTitle: New design of ultra-wideband bandpass filter using metamaterial resonator
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: An ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter based on composite right/left handed (CRLH) transmission line is presented in this paper. The bandwidth of the filter can be widen by the high-low-high step-impedance section and two novel interdigital capacitors of the CRLH transmission line. The common short circuited inductive stub of two capacitors exhibits stopband rejection level greater than 30 dB at both the lower and upper band edges. Numerical simulations using ANSYS HFSS reveal 3-dB bandwidth of 7.5 GHz from 3.1 GHz to 10.6 GHz and the average insertion loss of 0.5 dB while the return loss of more than 18 dB in passband. In addition, a DGS structure is proposed to create a notched band in order to attenuate some undesired signals such as local area networks (WLAN) in the UWB band. The proposed filter will be useful in the wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Modeling Rabi oscillation by rigorously solving Maxwell-Schrödinger equation
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: When an atom (or two-level system) is illuminated by a coherent beam of photons, it will cyclically absorb photons and re-emit them by stimulated emission, which is called Rabi oscillation. By using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, Maxwell-Schrödinger equation is solved for modeling the Rabi oscillation. The proposed method is compared with the existing approximate theoretical models. It is found that these approximate models break down in certain cases where a rigorous self-consistent numerical approach is needed. This work is helpful for the EM simulation of emerging nanodevices or next-generation quantum electrodynamic systems.

articleTitle: Microstrip antenna for UWB with WLAN band rejection
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a compact ultra-wide band antenna with band-notched characteristics. The antenna has stable radiation pattern with return loss below − 10 dB except for 5.15–5.825 GHz, which is the band allocated to WLAN by IEEE 802.11a and HIPERLAN/2, achieved by inserting a U-shaped slot in radiating element.

articleTitle: A discontinuous Galerkin surface integral equation method based domain decomposition method using the CN/LT basis functions
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: An integral equation domain decomposition method based on discontinuous Galerkin is proposed. The continuity of the induced electrical current at the boundaries between subdomains is enforced by discontinuous Galerkin penalty term. Elemental-wised CN/LT basis functions are used for expanding induced electrical current. Using CN/LT basis functions results in a much smaller linear system than using L2 basis functions, therefore the linear system obtained by using CN/LT basis functions can be solved more efficiently. Furthermore, the local characteristics of CN/LT basis functions provide the flexibility in geometry modeling and efficiency in mesh generation. The numerical results show good accuracy and the induced current satisfy the continuity condition on the artificial interface between subdomains.

articleTitle: Studies on satellite antenna gain measurement system based on comparison method
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the satellite antenna gain measurement system based on comparison method. Gain is the most important performance parameter of an antenna. However, in many practical situations it is not possible to measure or calculate the gain of an antenna. Comparison method in this paper means using standard antenna to calculate the gain of antenna under test (AUT), which has advantages in accuracy, operability and range of applicability. Examples of measuring gain of 7.3 m diameter satellite antenna are given. Comparative analysis between comparison method and half-power beamwidth method, which is international general method for antenna gain measurement, is carried out. The analysis shows that comparison method is feasible.

articleTitle: LTE/WiFi coexistence in unlicensed bands by HLBT mechanism
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: With the growth of data demand in Long Term Evolution (LTE), licensed frequency bands are becoming increasingly crowded. Implementing LTE system to unlicensed frequency bands, called Licensed-Assisted Access (LAA), has been raised to solve the problem. However, there exist other wireless networks in the unlicensed bands, such as 802.11p system. LAA system needs to avoid interference with other wireless systems in the same frequency band. In this paper, Listen-Before- Talk (LBT) mechanism, which is raised to realize the coexistence between LAA system and WiFi system, has been simulated. Moreover, a novel hybrid LBT (HLBT) mechanism has been discussed and compared with LBT mechanism. HLBT mechanism includes two operating modes, which are designed for different channel situations, and switches between them adaptively. The simulation results illustrate that both LBT and HLBT mechanisms can make LAA system coexist with other systems, and HLBT mechanism performs better.

articleTitle: Design of a dual-band printed monopole MIMO antenna with high isolation
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: A dual band multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with high isolation for LTE and WLAN has been presented in this paper. To improve the isolation of each element, the two elements are placed 180° apart on FR4 substrate (78×40 mm2). The simulated results show that the proposed MIMO antenna operates at the following frequency bands: 2.20– 3.15 GHz and 5.24–5.83 GHz while |S11|<10 dB, with a bandwidth of 950 MHz (lower band) and 590 MHz (upper band). The designed antenna has a minimum isolation of −20 dB in the lower band and −22.4 dB in the upper band. The maximum gain of each operating element is 3.52 dBi at 2.45 GHz and 4.24 dBi at 5.5 GHz. The measured results are agreement with the simulated results. The results show that the proposed MIMO antenna has a good characteristic in bandwidth, isolation and gain.

articleTitle: Improved gap waveguide PMC packaging for zeroth-order resonator
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 6th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a new metamaterial-based waveguide technology referred to as packaging gap waveguide, which is used to improve the performance of zeroth-order resonator (ZOR). In this approach, a lid of spiral nails used for perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) together with the ground plane of the substrate created a gap to suppress the power leakage problem of ZOR.
